First, given a WDN modeled by nonlinear differential-algebraic equations (NDAEs) consisting of transient flow dynamics as differential equation (DE) and conservation of water mass as algebraic equation (AE) and considering the pipe flow rates as states of the state-space (SS) representation, we extract a linearized system modeled by linear ordinary differential equations (LODEs) around the equilibrium (i.e., steady) flow rate vector. Second, treating pipe flow rates as SS nodes (states), we introduce a node centrality-based measure, namely \textit{vulnerability vector (VV)}, to rank the network pipes based on their influence on the dynamics and topology of the WDN in the case of input changes. In particular, the network's most and least influential pipes can be identified through such a centrality-based approach. This enables water engineers to understand the WDN's vulnerability better and effectively prioritize the maintenance and operational efforts on the most influential pipes within the WDN.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Adaptive PD-like Fault Tolerant Controller for a Class of Nonlinear Systems
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: The article presents a nonlinear adaptive control strategy for a class of feedback-linearizable systems subject to process faults and disturbance. The controller is derived through Lyapunov analysis and incorporates an adaptive proportional gain within a PD-like structure, preserving simplicity while providing nonlinear adaptive behavior. A residual-based gating mechanism activates the adaptation only when the tracking error exceeds a prescribed threshold, preventing unnecessary gain updates during nominal operation and improving robustness to noise. The proposed design yields uniform global ultimate boundedness of the closed-loop signals, with explicit expressions for the steady-state tracking bound. Practical tuning guidelines for the adaptive parameters and Lyapunov matrix selection are provided to ensure consistent gating behavior. Simulations on a precision positioning system illustrate effective compensation of process faults, rapid gain escalation during degraded conditions, and smooth reversion to nominal performance, demonstrating that the method enhances fault tolerance while retaining the structural simplicity of PD control.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Nonlinear Fault Tolerant Control of Wind Turbine Pitch Systems: A Comparative Study
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Electro-hydraulic pitch systems account for about one fifth of wind-turbine failures, motivating the development of resilient control strategies for fault mitigation. The study considers a large set of robust nonlinear control designs of different feedback principles and architectures, and assesses their fault-tolerant capabilities in comparison to each other and against the industrial standard, i.e. the Proportional-Integral (PI) controller. The implementation and tuning of each scheme is based on a high-fidelity simulator to ensure nominal performance, whereas each controller is deployed unchanged on an experimental apparatus that includes a full-scale electro-hydraulic pitch system. The comparative evaluation of the considered fault-tolerant solutions is carried out through several tests that cover nominal operation and twenty-five representative fault scenarios, including sensor, process, and actuator faults. The analysis highlights the trade-off between performance preservation under faults and increased actuator chattering. The experimental results show that introducing a dynamic input-reconstruction module into the design of the nonlinear controllers significantly reduces actuator chatter without compromising their fault-tolerant properties.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: LACART: Lookahead-Augmented Collision Avoidance and Reference Tracking Strategies for Safety-Critical Robots
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Autonomous racing provides a demanding testbed for collision avoidance under tight geometric and computational constraints. Building on a recent conference contribution and a master's dissertation, LACART combines lookahead-based control barrier functions (CBFs), a relaxed control Lyapunov function (CLF), and quadratic programming (QP) to modify nominal vehicle commands for obstacle avoidance and reference tracking. The method handles circular obstacles and track boundaries in a common optimisation layer. Comparative simulation results against Huang \emph{et al.} \cite{r9} show similar full-track paths and lower median computation times: 0.31 versus 0.33 ms per step and 0.023 versus 0.025 ms per QP solve. The dissertation further demonstrates a 1:43-scale vehicle with camera-based estimation and wireless actuation at a reported 25 Hz control rate. We identify the conditions linking lookahead-point clearance to body clearance, illustrate hardware limitations, and propose a recorded demonstration of safety intervention and recovery. The contribution targets ground-robot collision avoidance and real-time safety monitoring.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: A Novel Algorithm to Simulate Conductance-based Neuronal Networks
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Conductance-based models are central to neurophysiology and neuromorphic engineering, yet their simulation scales poorly to large networks. We study and analyze an iterative solver that operates in signal space. Each iteration reduces to $N$ decoupled scalar linear time-varying differential equations, one per neuron, which are solved in parallel and in closed form. The solver admits two complementary interpretations: a variable metric forward-backward splitting method, rooted in operator theory, and a waveform relaxation quasi-Newton method, rooted in circuit simulation. We prove uniform and superlinear convergence, with a bound that reflects the conductance structure of the dynamics. The algorithm is illustrated on the classical Hodgkin--Huxley neuron and on networks of up to 5000 neurons.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Beyond Feasibility: Efficient and Robust On-Device Localization with UWB Concurrent Transmissions
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Concurrent transmissions (CTX) enable an ultra-wideband (UWB) tag to range to, or self-localize from, multiple nodes with a single frame reception, significantly improving update rate and energy efficiency compared to traditional approaches. Prior work demonstrated the concept feasibility via prototypes whose real-world applicability is however hindered by many limitations, notably including their inability to directly execute on UWB tags and to cope with interfering UWB signals. We address these limitations in two ways. First, we redesign the core CTX techniques to enable a fast and efficient execution on resource-constrained MCUs without sacrificing accuracy. Second, we leverage the new features in the IEEE 802.15.4z standard to achieve robustness to interference from other UWB devices and enable tags to dynamically select which anchors to use, two crucial and unexplored capabilities in CTX-based systems. We quantitatively evaluate our approach experimentally in two real-world testbeds with different characteristics. We first analyze our new techniques individually, offering an in-depth discussion of design choices and performance trade-offs. Then, we embed all our techniques into a CTX-based system enabling a tag to self-localize entirely on-device, unlocking gains up to 44% in runtime and 85% in energy efficiency compared to traditional approaches.
Systems and Control (EESS).comment: Submitted to the IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Data-driven representation of continuous-time linear time-invariant behaviors via Hankel integral operators
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: We present a data-driven representation of the finite-horizon behavior of deterministic controllable continuous-time LTI systems. We first introduce a notion of persistency of excitation for continuous-time signals that does not require the signal to be differentiable. We then show that, when the input is persistently exciting in this sense, the closure of the range of a Hankel integral operator built from a single input-output trajectory equals the behavior of the system over a finite time horizon. This result provides a nonparametric representation of system trajectories directly in terms of measured data, without requiring an explicit parametric model of the system.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Characterization of the Frequency-Current Curve of First-Order High-Pass Neurons
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: A spiking model, called the High-Pass (HP) model, has recently been proposed as a minimal excitable primitive. This model is composed of a static activation function, usually a sigmoid, in positive feedback with a high-pass filter. The HP model enters a tonic spiking regime whenever its input lies in the high-gain zone of the sigmoid, where the sigmoid's slope exceeds 1. In neuroscience, the frequency-current (FI) curve is the standard way of characterizing the tonic spiking regime of a neuron. So far, the FI curve of the HP model has been characterized analytically only for specific sigmoids, and has otherwise been computed through simulation. These simulations are computationally heavy, since simulating neurons requires solving a stiff system of differential equations. This paper bridges this gap by analytically characterizing the FI curve of the HP model with a first-order high-pass filter, for a broad class of sigmoid functions. The FI curve of the first-order HP model can be computed by solving two input-independent equations and evaluating two input-dependent integrals, with no need to simulate the model itself. A spiking primitive is said to be Type I (resp. Type II) if tonic spiking starts at a zero (resp. non-zero) frequency. This paper also shows that, for the HP model, the type depends solely on the local shape of the sigmoid at the outer edges of its high-gain zone. A sharp corner, where the derivative approaches a value strictly smaller than 1 from the outside, yields a Type I primitive. A locally twice differentiable corner, with a bounded second derivative and a derivative approaching 1 at the edge, yields a Type II primitive.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: RADAR Perception for Dynamic Obstacle Avoidance onboard small-scale Quadrotor UAVs
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Fast dynamic obstacle avoidance (DOA) on uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs) demands not only low-latency control and actuation but also reliable, long-range perception to detect obstacles and estimate their motion in time to maneuver. We present, to the best of our knowledge, the first mmWave RADAR-based perception-and-control system for fast onboard DOA. We derive and analyze latency and spatial bounds that relate sensing range, relative speed, and control delay, yielding sufficient conditions for successful avoidance. We further extend prior latency analyses to include the decision latency of the tracker and trigger to evaluate them per trial. Our computationally efficient system combines a lightweight interacting multiple models (IMM) tracker with a control-barrier functions (CBF) controller that directly outputs evasive accelerations. In 300 throw experiments spanning three object sizes and varying visibility (light and dark), it achieves mean position errors of at most 0.15 m, 0.93m, and 0.87m in the x, y, and z directions, with a similar spread in 90 experiments in smoke. An onboard implementation on a Raspberry Pi 4B demonstrates real-time feasibility with an end-to-end processing latency of approximately 14ms per RADAR frame and a system latency of 75ms from first detection to the avoidance command. The UAV successfully avoided obstacles in all 20 tethered indoor flights and all 39 untethered outdoor avoidance maneuvers across three ball sizes, during both hover and forward flights at up to 5m/s with measured closing speeds up to 14.6m/s.
Systems and Control (EESS).comment: Preprint. This work has been submitted for possible publication and is currently under review

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Data-Driven Continuous-Time LQR: Linking Reinforcement Learning and Behavioral System Theory
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Behavioral system theory and reinforcement learning (RL) have independently developed data-driven approaches to the continuous-time LQR problem, yet their respective methods have largely evolved in separation. We connect these two adjacent lines of work by studying their data-driven parameterizations, namely a closed-loop (CL) parameterization from behavioral system theory and an integral RL (IRL) parameterization. The CL parameterization characterizes the closed-loop system via a matrix that satisfies equality constraints. While this parameterization has been extensively studied for discrete-time systems, we adapt key results to the continuous-time setting and develop a policy iteration (PI) scheme, derive an algebraic Riccati equation, and introduce an alternative convex program. The IRL parameterization utilizes off-policy data to perform policy evaluation, which is used for PI or value iteration. Within the IRL framework, we derive a policy gradient flow and propose convex programs for the LQR problem. Finally, we provide a unified treatment of these parameterizations that enables a systematic understanding of existing approaches, and clarifies their structural relationships.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Safety Blind Spot in Remote Driving: Considerations for Risk Assessment of Connection Loss Fallback Strategies
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: As part of the overall goal of driverless road vehicles, remote driving is a major emerging field of research of its own. Current remote driving concepts for public road traffic often establish a fallback strategy of immediate braking to a standstill in the event of a connection loss. This may seem like the most logical option when human control of the vehicle is lost. However, our simulation results from hundreds of scenarios based on naturalistic traffic scenes indicate high collision rates for any immediate substantial deceleration to a standstill in urban settings. We show that such a fallback strategy can result in a SOTIF-relevant hazard, raising the question whether this design decision is acceptable. Therefore, from a safety perspective, we call this problem a safety blind spot, as safety analyses in this regard seem to be very rare. In this article, we first present a simulation on a naturalistic dataset that shows a high probability of collision in the described case. Second, we discuss the severity of the resulting potential rear-end collisions and provide an even more severe example by including a large commercial vehicle in the potential collision.
Systems and Control (EESS).comment: This work has been submitted for possible publication. Copyright may be transferred without notice, after which this version may no longer be accessible

Systems and Control (EESS).title: An Inspection Game for Monitor Design Against GNSS Timing Attacks in Synchronous Islanding
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Phasor measurement units (PMUs) take their time from GNSS, so a spoofer that slowly drags a receiver clock rotates the reported phase without touching the power waveform. The threat is acute in synchronous islanding, where a controller keeps an islanded generator in phase with the grid, using one PMU on each side of an open breaker, so that the two can be reconnected at any moment: a differential clock bias of about $0.56$\,ms can make the controller hold the generator $10^\circ$ out of phase while it reports perfect synchronism. We cast the defense as a zero-sum inspection game. The defender, as inspector, chooses its timing monitors and audits the clocks periodically; the attacker, as inspectee, drags the two clocks to an unsafe bias by the next audit; the payoff is the evidence, the Kullback--Leibler divergence between the probability laws of the defender's record under attack and under normal operation. Our central result is that the evidence equals the cost of the cheapest innocent explanation of the attacked record. This single identity predicts which monitors work, turns the attacker's best response into a strictly convex quadratic program, and turns the defender's design into a convex program with a saddle point. Pairing explanations, which bound the evidence from above, with test statistics, which bound it from below, certifies audit periods in which every successful attack leaves at least a threshold of evidence. On a 50\,Hz island, these evidence-based periods, at the matched-test threshold, are up to 8.4 times as long as those of a rule that checks each monitor separately, and the case study favors placing the better oscillator on the utility side of the breaker.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: An Optimal Power-Flow Grouping Topology for Single-Isolation-Stage Multi-Output Solid-State Transformers
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Electric-vehicle dc fast-charging stations and data centers require multiple high-power dc outputs with independently varying demands. Conventional multi-output solid-state transformers typically establish a common dc bus and use downstream dc/dc converters for port-level regulation and, where required, galvanic isolation. A single-isolation-stage solid-state transformer can eliminate this additional high-power interface stage by directly forming multiple isolated outputs from its submodule dc/dc stages. However, because one submodule is generally insufficient for an individual output port, multiple submodules must be connected in parallel, while inter-submodule balancing circuits redistribute power under unbalanced loading. The submodule grouping therefore determines the internal balancing-power paths. Sequential grouping can create long transfer paths and accumulated balancing power, increasing current stress and losses. This paper proposes an optimal power-flow grouping topology that interleaves submodules assigned to different output ports, thereby localizing power redistribution and reducing the power processed by the balancing circuits. Analytical models quantify the required balancing power and its reduction relative to sequential grouping. A coordinated submodule-bypass strategy is also developed, and the remaining output-power capability under different fault scenarios is evaluated. A six-submodule prototype validates the proposed topology. Under the same highly unbalanced operating conditions, the proposed topology reduces the maximum submodule dc-link voltage difference by 63\% and the peak balancing current by 14.5%, while improving the measured efficiency by approximately 5.6% at rated power. Stable post-fault operation is also experimentally demonstrated.
Systems and Control (EESS).comment: 13 pages, 19 figures. Submitted to IEEE for possible publication

Systems and Control (EESS).title: DC-Link Voltage Regulation in a Single-Isolation-Stage Multioutput Solid-State Transformer for Wide-Range DC Outputs
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Single-isolation-stage solid-state transformers with balancing circuits eliminate an additional downstream dc--dc conversion stage. However, the remaining isolated converters must directly accommodate a wide output-voltage range. This paper investigates variable dc-link voltage operation of a single-isolation-stage multioutput SST to ease this requirement. Coordinated cascaded H-bridge modulation and embedded four-switch balancing circuits support intentionally unequal submodule dc-link voltages, allowing the isolated-converter input voltages to be adjusted according to the output requirements. The achievable voltage range is determined by relating the required balancing power to the BC transfer capability within the available CHB switching windows, subject to modulation and peak and rms current limits. The analysis quantifies the range extension provided by BC operation beyond modulation alone. For a single-phase-shift dual-active-bridge converter, input-voltage following within this range reduces the calculated peak current and extends the ideal zero-voltage-switching region compared with fixed input. Experiments on a six-submodule SST prototype demonstrate unequal dc-link voltage operation and inter-submodule power exchange. Experiments result on DAB demonstrate reduced current stress and improved efficiency with voltage following.
Systems and Control (EESS).comment: Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Power Electronics (TPEL) for possible publication

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Reconciling European Electricity Data with Diffusion Priors Learned from Observations Alone
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: The ENTSO-E Transparency Platform publishes generation, load, and cross-border power flows for European bidding zones. The values carry undocumented errors and violate energy conservation, and data reconciliation consists in correcting them to satisfy that balance. In this work, we formulate data reconciliation as Bayesian inference. Classical methods implicitly take a uniform prior, which we replace with a diffusion model estimated from the observations alone by empirical-Bayes expectation-maximization. The resulting posterior is sampled with a guided process whose projection step makes every sample satisfy the balance exactly. On synthetic systems of six to thirty-five bidding zones, built from ENTSO-E resource-adequacy data, the diffusion prior gives the most accurate reconciliation, increasingly so as the system grows. Its credible intervals are calibrated or conservative, and it remains the most accurate under a misspecified noise covariance. Finally, when the generation of entire zones goes unreported, the classical methods fail while the learned prior recovers it from cross-zone structure.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Voltage Sensitivity-Based Fair Allocation of Operating Envelopes in Distribution Networks
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Operating envelopes (OEs) define the admissible active and reactive power injections of distributed energy resources while respecting distribution network limits. In unbalanced low-voltage feeders, OEs based only on voltage magnitude and thermal limits may overestimate available flexibility because they neglect power quality requirements. This paper develops a three-phase unbalanced AC optimal power flow framework to compute coupled active and reactive power OEs while enforcing limits on the voltage unbalance factor (VUF). It also proposes a fairness mechanism based on voltage sensitivities to allocate available flexibility among multiple photovoltaic (PV) units. The proposed mechanism is compared with lexicographic max--min fairness as a benchmark for equitable resource allocation. Case studies on unbalanced test feeders evaluate how VUF constraints change the feasible operating region of PV units. The results show how VUF constraints affect feasible flexibility and demonstrate that the proposed voltage sensitivity-based mechanism is nearly six times faster than lexicographic max-min fairness.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Probabilistic Sequential Safety for Stochastic Dynamical Systems
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: In this letter, we investigate a notion of probabilistic safety for a stochastic dynamical system. Standard safety notions are based on the idea that an unsafe region of the state-space must be avoided at each instant. In contrast, we study a sequential safety notion which is based on avoiding a tuple of target regions of the state-space. The proposed safety notion is inspired by many practical systems, ranging from modeling jailbreak attacks in large language models (LLMs) to predicting hazardous chemical reactions. In solving the sequential safety problem, we solve a sequential reachability problem for a stochastic dynamical system.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Controlled Excitation for Identification of Nonlinear Systems with Saturated Outputs
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: We consider nonlinear systems whose measured output is the product of an unknown matrix and a known saturation function of the unmeasured state. Generating excitation that allows the matrix to be recovered from the output is challenging when the dynamics are largely unknown. We exploit saturation to construct this excitation. Under a geometric accessibility condition, we derive explicit open-loop controls that drive the state into regions where the saturation takes prescribed values. For componentwise saturations, this condition holds generically with as few as two independent control directions. The controls require no state measurement and only partial knowledge of the dynamics, with no information on the structure of its nonlinear part. The resulting regressor is known in advance, and the unknown matrix is recovered exactly by a closed-form regression. Under stronger structural assumptions and with sufficiently many independent outputs, an output feedback tracks prescribed reference trajectories within the unsaturated region to arbitrary accuracy and permits exact state recovery. Suitably chosen references then also enable exact identification of linearly parameterized (nonlinear) dynamics. We analyze robustness to measurement noise and illustrate the method numerically in the presence of both measurement and dynamical noise.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Real-Time Nonlinear Mixed-Integer Model Predictive Control With Horizon-Tail Relaxations
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Model predictive control (MPC) of nonlinear systems with discrete decisions leads to mixed-integer nonlinear programs (MINLPs) whose combinatorial complexity often prevents real-time deployment. In this paper, we propose a decomposition-based MPC method that reorders and reduces computations to shorten the delay between receiving a state measurement and applying the control input. Before the measurement arrives, we solve a continuous relaxation of the MINLP at a predicted state and construct a mixed-integer quadratic program (MIQP). Once the measured state is available, we solve the MIQP that reconstructs the discrete controls and simultaneously performs one sequential quadratic programming step toward the corresponding nonlinear solution. To reduce the combinatorial complexity in the horizon length, we either fix the integer controls or relax their integrality over the prediction horizon tail, while retaining an integer-feasible first control input. We derive error bounds relating the nonlinear objective values obtained with the horizon-tail approximations to the optimal value of the original mixed-integer problem. In a data center cooling example, the proposed method reduces mean feedback computation time by 94% relative to a state-of-the-art MINLP method with a total closed-loop cost difference of less than 1%.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Circuit Theory-Informed AI for Condition Monitoring in Power Electronics
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Artificial intelligence for power electronics is evolving toward a deeper comprehension of system intrinsic behaviors and dynamics. As a novel integration of neural computation and electric circuits, spike-based neuromorphic computing offers promising potential in high energy efficiency and adaptability for data-driven applications. Building on the latency-coding principles, this article proposes a framework for data-light condition monitoring that relies solely on three-phase AC current measurements. The AC current signals are encoded as membrane potentials of RC-based spiking neurons, which are inherently compatible with spiking neural networks that can effectively facilitate the estimation of device parameters. Case studies are presented to validate the performances, while constraints and further optimizations are also evaluated and discussed, and future extensions of the methodology are provided.
Systems and Control (EESS).comment: The manuscript has been accepted for publication in the Proceedings of 2026 IEEE Design Methodologies Conference (DMC 2026)

Systems and Control (EESS).title: An Enhanced Submodule for Modular Multilevel Converters With DC Fault-Clearing Capability
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Modular multilevel converter (MMC) has been successfully applied in various power electronic systems owing to its high efficiency, scalability, and superior output performance. Although the half-bridge submodule (HBSM) is widely used in MMCs for its structural simplicity, it is incapable of handling direct-current (DC) short-circuit faults. The diode-clamp submodule (DCSM) addresses this limitation by providing DC fault ride-through capability. However, because its two identical capacitors are connected in series, the equivalent capacitance is halved. To overcome this drawback, an enhanced SM is proposed in this paper. For the same energy storage capacity, the proposed SM reduces the total required capacitance by 75% compared with the DCSM. In addition, the proposed SM requires one fewer diode than the DCSM, thereby lowering the overall MMC capital cost. The topology and the operating modes of the proposed SM are described in detail, and its functionality is experimentally validated. The results demonstrate that the proposed SM can suppress DC fault currents and restore normal operation without additional external protection devices.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Safe Circumnavigation on Heterogeneous Orbits: A Range-Only HOCBF-QP Framework for Nonholonomic Multi-Agent Systems
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Circumnavigating a stationary target with a team of robots requires each robot to hold its own standoff distance, to stay evenly spaced from its neighbours, and to avoid collisions with the target and with each other at every instant. The task becomes arduous when the robots are assigned different orbital radii, as their sensors or roles may demand. This paper presents a safety-critical control framework for this problem. Each robot commands both its acceleration and its turn-rate, measures only its distance to the target, and exchanges information only with its two ring neighbours. The design has three features. First, a structural property of the model lets one control law serve every robot regardless of its assigned radius. Second, the acceleration drives each radius exactly to its target, while the turn-rate balances the formation with the neighbours. Third, a higher-order control-barrier-function quadratic program enforces target, geofence, and inter-robot safety on both inputs at once; it leaves the nominal controller untouched away from the constraints and stays valid while the unmeasured range rate is still being estimated. Simulations confirm these guarantees. In a comparison, the closest existing multi-orbit design, even with full state information, violates both the target standoff and the inter-robot margin, whereas the proposed controller does not.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Fair Selection of Generalized Nash Equilibria: A Comparability Perspective
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Generalized Nash equilibrium (GNE) problems model self-interested agents coupled through their costs and shared constraints, and arise throughout control applications that allocate a scarce common resource. Such problems typically admit a continuum of equilibria, so any implementation must \emph{select} one. This selection is not neutral: it decides how the cost of the shared constraint is distributed among the agents, a decision often expected to be fair. The variational GNE (v-GNE), which charges all agents a uniform shadow price, is the conventional choice and is frequently advocated as fair. Through the lens of \emph{comparability} from social choice theory, we show that the GNE set itself requires no inter-agent comparability of costs, whereas the v-GNE implicitly assumes cardinal unit comparability, one of the stronger notions. We then introduce the fair GNE (f-GNE), which selects an equilibrium by explicitly optimizing a fairness metric matched to the comparability at hand, and give constructive routes to compute it for single-constraint and linear-quadratic games. An electric-vehicle charging game serves as a running example throughout this self-contained tutorial.
Systems and Control (EESS).comment: Book chapter, 25 pages, 4 figures. To appear in Socio-Inspired and Socially Aware Control for Complex Systems, Springer

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Supporting Data Center Grid Integration via Co-Optimized Battery Energy Storage Sizing and Capacity Allocation
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Interconnecting large data centers can be delayed by grid requirements on demand flexibility, ramping limits, and ride-through performance. This paper proposes an optimization-based framework to size a Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) that accelerates data center grid integration by providing BESS capacity required to meet selected flexibility and grid-support requirements. The model co-optimizes BESS power rating and energy capacity while allocating capability across three services: (i) demand response over a specified duration, (ii) mitigation of high-magnitude, high-frequency load fluctuations through reserved active power with zero net state-of-charge change, and (iii) voltage support via reactive power capability at the point of common coupling. Minute-level operational scheduling enforces state-of-charge feasibility and load ramp constraints, and incorporates a controllable queue of delay-insensitive computing tasks to enhance flexibility. A case study using a real data center load profile demonstrates the proposed method and quantifies the BESS power-energy requirements and operational trade-offs needed to satisfy the multi-service constraints, providing practical guidance for interconnection planning and deployment.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Grid-Oriented Probabilistic Load Forecasting for AI Data Centers
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Probabilistic load forecasts for AI data centers need to represent both uncertainty under changing workloads and temporal dependence to support grid operations. This paper develops an open, grid-oriented benchmark using measured GPU power from a 448-GPU AI cluster. Forecasts are evaluated through four stages: probabilistic prediction, online uncertainty calibration, temporal scenario generation, and horizon-wide reserve sizing. Following a change in cluster utilization, a quantile LightGBM forecast achieves only 63.4% coverage for a nominal 90% interval, while online regime-conditioned calibration increases coverage to 87.3%. Even with well-calibrated marginal forecasts, independent sampling produces unrealistic ramp distributions and excessive reserve procurement. Reconstructing temporal dependence from historical forecast errors reduces the discrepancy in ramp statistics and lowers realized reserve cost by 7.4-10.6% across three forecasting tasks. These findings show that marginal forecast quality alone is insufficient for operational decisions and motivate joint evaluation of calibration, temporal structure, and decision outcomes.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Defense Filters for Robust Learning of Partially Observed Dynamical Systems
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Robust estimation of unknown system dynamics from partial observations under attack is a core challenge in learning for control, increasingly critical in multi-agent networks subject to adversarial data poisoning. Existing methods either require highly restrictive assumptions on the adversary or yield weak error bounds. In this paper, we consider identifying partially observed linear dynamical systems subject to adversarial attacks with an attack probability $p < 0.5$ at each time. We propose a defense-filtering framework leveraging knowledge of the observation matrix to construct a defense filter satisfying full column rank and subspace separability conditions, which enables the evaluation of a single-attack scenario against observed data. Using this framework, we analyze the constrained $\ell_2$-norm estimator and establish finite-sample error bounds for recovering the Markov parameter matrix up to a linear transformation. This is the first approach to provide provable system identification guarantees via a defense filter for partially observed systems subject to harsh environments where the attack probability approaches $0.5$.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: A Measure-Theoretic Formulation of Behavioral Systems
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Ensemble control specifies probability laws on admissible trajectories, including their temporal dependence. Starting from an arbitrary closed behavior, we organize its laws into a framework that connects standard probability-measure geometry, occupation-measure control, and data-driven trajectory parametrization. Classical convexity and extreme-point properties describe the feasible laws, while classical Bellman duality governs additive control objectives. On compact state and input spaces, full-path constrained duality for continuous trajectory functions gives primal attainment and zero gap whenever feasible. For controllable linear time-invariant systems, the noise-free Fundamental Lemma yields an equivalent law-level Hankel factorization, with a canonical pseudoinverse lift. The factorization transfers trajectory-law constraints exactly to coefficient space and connects them to covariance control. Explicit noisy-Hankel bounds quantify subspace approximation for second-moment-bounded laws under known rank and Gaussian output measurement noise. Numerical studies include a nonlinear reset problem whose nonadjacent correlation constraint requires temporal memory, covariance-constrained optimization, and noisy-data policy evaluation. Known transition kernels provide a further structural perspective through history-conditional consistency.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Extending Grid Foundation Models for Phasor-Domain Dynamic Simulation
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Grid Foundation Models (GridFMs) are emerging as a powerful framework for learning and transferring knowledge across power grids and grid analysis tasks. This work extends GridFMs from steady-state analysis to dynamic simulation. We present DynGridFM, which uses component-wise tokenization and a structured latent operator to learn shared dynamic representations across heterogeneous grids and enable transfer to unseen systems. Pretrained on nine grids, DynGridFM is adapted to a held-out 48-machine grid, where fine-tuning on 64 trajectories achieves accuracy comparable to training from scratch on 128. On a single GPU, it achieves 924x to 1232x speedup over numerical simulators on one CPU core.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: An Ultra-Low-Noise Tunable TIA in 45nm Silicon Photonics for Electro-Optical Ultrasound Data Acquisition
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: This paper presents the design and experimental characterization of a 32-channel, WDM-compatible electronic-photonic receiver array fabricated in the GlobalFoundries 45nm monolithic silicon photonics process. Optimized for miniaturized, millimeter-scale electro-optical ultrasound data acquisition probes for broadband photo-acoustic imaging (PAI), the chip utilizes integrated micro-ring resonator (MRR) demultiplexers and photodiode (PD) arrays to decode multi-wavelength acoustic signals outside the body. This work focuses specifically on the comprehensive characterization of the receiver front-end, evaluating both the optical WDM filter bank and the transimpedance amplifier (TIA) performance. Monolithic co-integration minimizes critical photodiode-to-TIA interface parasitics. The TIA incorporates a DC-offset cancellation loop that compensates for photodiode-induced offset currents while providing tunable low-frequency cutoff control over a range of 30 kHz to 1.5 MHz. This tunability enables effective suppression of flicker noise and improves overall signal integrity. The front-end achieves the peak transimpedance gain of 144 dB$Ω$ while maintaining an ultra-low input-referred noise current density of $1\text{ pA}/\sqrt{\text{Hz}}$, demonstrating a highly scalable architecture for high-sensitivity intravascular and endobronchial imaging.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Sensing-Based Communication: A Non-Orthogonal Passive Reflection Framework for ISAC
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: While integrating uplink without disrupting the primary downlink remains a critical challenge for existing reflective communication systems, this paper proposes a non-orthogonal passive integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) mechanism termed Sensing-based Communication. Originating from and validated within an optical retro-reflective system, this mechanism possesses an underlying wave-agnostic architecture with the potential to be generalized across other physical modalities. It leverages incident downlink signals for parasitic modulation via passive tags. By relying solely on fundamental on-off keying (OOK) reflection, the tag unifies the reflective sensing channel and the uplink communication channel, and simultaneously achieves both sensing and duplex communication. Consequently, our approach introduces uplink capability without sacrificing the downlink data rate or consuming additional spectrum resources. At the receiver, we design a joint decoding architecture combining cross-correlation computation and successive interference cancelation (SIC) to fully exploit the degrees of freedom in broadband signals for multi-user interference suppression. We derive closed-form expressions for the interference and bit error rate (BER) assuming zero-mean Gaussian signals. Using an experimental testbed, we validate the pivotal theoretical finding, the scaling relationship of SINR with signal bandwidth and cross-correlation time--where linear regression yields a strong goodness-of-fit with $R^2 = 0.9688$. Furthermore, evaluations under noise-like orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) waveforms exhibit high consistency between theoretical derivations and simulation data ($R^2 = 0.9372$, mean absolute percentage error, $\text{MAPE} = 14\%$), confirming the model's accuracy and waveform generalizability.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Learning-Oriented Fault-Tolerant Control for UAVs with Time-Varying Fault Estimation
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: The increasing deployment of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in safety-critical applications has created a growing demand for control strategies that remain reliable in the presence of actuator and sensor faults. This paper presents a fault-tolerant control framework that combines constructive mathematical modeling, proportional--integral (PI) fault estimation, and learning-oriented control. A nonlinear quadcopter model is first developed using both the Newton--Euler and Euler--Lagrange formulations, from which a discrete-time linear model is derived for observer and controller design. A PI observer is then proposed to estimate actuator and sensor faults, with exponential estimation-error convergence established for constant faults in the absence of disturbances and ultimate boundedness established for slowly time-varying faults under bounded disturbances. The estimated fault signals are incorporated into an active fault-tolerant control architecture together with a Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) controller, which is trained using only the yaw channel and subsequently applied to improve closed-loop tracking performance. Numerical simulations illustrate the observer's estimation performance under constant and slowly time-varying faults, including bounded disturbances, and the tracking performance of the integrated controller under multiple actuator and sensor fault scenarios. The proposed framework combines model-based fault estimation with learning-based control to improve fault accommodation and tracking performance in UAV systems.
Systems and Control (EESS).comment: This is an extended version of the paper published in the proceedings of IEEE CoDIT

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Mobility Information Capacity of Multi-Robot Systems: Safety-Aware Maneuver Design
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Multiple robots operating in shared workspaces must adjust their speed, direction, and trajectories to coordinate with one another and respond to changing tasks and disturbances. The available maneuver freedom depends on the dynamics, uncertainty, and safety margins, even for a fixed fleet size and workspace. However, robot count, workspace occupancy, and task throughput do not quantify how much the fleet can vary its motion or how reliably these variations can be observed. We develop a mobility information capacity (MIC) framework that jointly characterizes these two aspects. Mobility information is defined as the mutual information between a joint maneuver sequence and its noisy trajectory observation, and MIC maximizes this quantity under maneuver-resource constraints. For a linear Gaussian maneuver-to-observation model with feedback dynamics, we characterize the finite-horizon information benchmark and derive its stationary long-horizon spectral limit, accounting for heterogeneous mobility gains, colored uncertainty, and temporally coupled maneuver costs. We further map workspace-boundary, inter-robot separation, and actuator chance constraints into coupled maneuver-covariance restrictions and derive conditions under which covariance optimization reduces to resource allocation across mobility modes. Finite joint maneuver codebooks are then constructed through individual risk screening and noise-whitened trajectory separation, with bounds linking sequence recovery error and achieved information to the capacity benchmarks. An aerial-robot simulation study evaluates spectral convergence, safety-aware allocation, finite-codebook identification, and fleet-size scaling. The resulting framework complements occupancy and task-throughput measures by quantifying the maximum observable maneuver freedom supported by a mobility system.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Lipschitz-Guided Machine Learning Framework for Accelerating Transient Stability Analysis of Flexible Traction Power Supply Systems
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: The rapidly varying and moving train loads in electrified railways impose stringent requirements on the transient stability of flexible traction power supply systems (FTPSSs). However, the complex dynamic interactions among numerous traction substations (TSs) make it challenging for existing transient stability analysis (TSA) methods to achieve both high accuracy and computational efficiency. To bridge this gap, this paper proposes a Lipschitz-guided machine learning framework that leverages Lipschitz continuity to restructure the transient stability verification of FTPSSs. By replacing computationally intensive satisfiability modulo theories (SMT) solvers with a deterministic algebraic check on a finite mesh, the proposed method ensures the Lyapunov conditions between mesh points without simplifications of the FTPSS dynamics. Validated on FTPSSs with three to five TSs through extensive case studies, the proposed framework accelerates training by up to 12 times compared with SMT-based neural Lyapunov methods and certifies the five-TS system. Furthermore, the proposed framework achieves up to a 33.5-fold increase in the estimated region of attraction (ROA) compared with linear matrix inequality.This advancement provides an efficient TSA solution for droop-controlled FTPSSs.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Governing Well in the Algorithmic Age: The Foundations of Digital Statecraft
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: The digital substrate - data, algorithms, infrastructure, platforms, applications - is being governed without adequate conceptual foundations. The ability and legitimacy required to govern this substrate, and to govern with it, are simultaneously misaligned, contested, and structurally absent. We introduce digital statecraft as the organising concept for this emerging field, arguing that 'digital' reconstitutes the statecraft question rather than merely extending its domain. The concept operates on two dimensions - statecraft over digital systems, concerning the authority and capacity of the state in relation to the digital substrate itself, and statecraft with digital systems, concerning the deployment of algorithmic tools as instruments of governing authority. And it rests on two foundational requirements, technical coherence and legitimate authority, that are genuinely in tension. We derive ten principles of digital statecraft from these foundations, each naming a condition whose absence produces an identifiable and structural governance failure: public interest first, human-machine complementarity, governability by design, systemic coherence, hybrid institutions, adaptive governance, human centricity and civic agency, accountable and traceable authority, judgment across time, and the non-delegable core. This article takes the state as the starting point, the institutional form that developed historically in response to the problem of effective and legitimate public governance, and the only current candidate for which the full set of legitimacy conditions is institutionally available. But the digital statecraft programme holds open a deeper question than just whether states can reform themselves: governing well in the algorithmic age may require rethinking the boundaries, scale, and affiliative basis of statehood itself.
authors: David Uriel Socol de la Osa

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Scalable Optimization for Mobility-Aware Coordinated Electric Vehicle Charging in Power Distribution Networks
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Rapid growth in electric-vehicle (EV) charging demand is placing increasing stress on power distribution networks (PDNs), whose hosting capacity is often limited and spatially uneven. Beyond demonstrating that coordination can help, this paper answers an open question that is central for planners: What is the maximal achievable benefit of EV charging demand flexibility from spatial and temporal shifting in reducing overload-driven distribution upgrades at a regional scale? We introduce MAC (Mobility-Aware Coordinated EV charging) to establish a credible upper bound, which entails rethinking charging flexibility around individual mobility, fusing travel itineraries with feeder-level hosting-capacity data, and solving population-scale optimization with spatio-temporal coupling to certified near-optimality. (i) MAC expands feasible scheduling by coupling charging decisions over the full mobility horizon. Instead of enforcing per-session energy recovery, it only requires the EV state-of-charge (SOC) to remain sufficient for upcoming trips. (ii) MAC is computationally scalable via an iterated price response (IPR) scheme. Each iteration posts a locational-temporal price, collects the fleet's best responses in parallel, and updates the price from the observed capacity shortage. Custom batched subproblem solvers remove the per-iteration bottleneck of solving millions of best responses. In a future-oriented 30% EV adoption scenario for the San Francisco Bay Area, MAC almost eliminates overload-driven upgrade needs relative to unmanaged charging. Comparing across the baseline spectrum, mobility-aware flexibility alone removes most of the overload, outperforming even fully coordinated session-based charging, and coordination on top suppresses most of the remainder. Both levers are thus essential, and the resulting best-case benchmarks provide references for PDN planning and operations.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Interconnections of Dissipative Networks Through a Dynamic Scattering Controller
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: The problem of modular scattering-based design of dissipative networks is addressed. Under basic assumptions imposed on subsystems, design of a dynamic scattering-based interconnection controller is proposed which guarantees that the resulting interconnection is internally stable and possesses the same set of basic properties as the individual subsystems. This enables iterative application of the developed technique, which allows for building of large-scale dissipative networks in a modular fashion. The proposed method provides substantial flexibility in the controller design as well as in the choice of input and output signals used for interconnections.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Dynamic Traffic Modeling using Equivalent Circuit Models
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: This paper presents an equivalent circuit model (ECM) for dynamic traffic modeling by exploiting analogies between electrical and transportation variables. Vehicle concentration is represented by capacitor voltage, while traffic flow is modeled using controllable current sources. The proposed formulation is shown to preserve the conservation and sending/receiving relationships of the spatially discretized Lighthill Whitham Richards traffic model. The framework is extended to restricted inflow, traffic signals, and two road merging and diverging scenarios. Validation against microscopic Simulation of Urban MObility (SUMO) simulations, involving traffic signals, two-road merging, and single-road diverging scenarios, demonstrates that the proposed ECM successfully reproduces the principal macroscopic traffic dynamics, including queue formation, backward congestion propagation, vehicle accumulation, saturation, and subsequent traffic recovery.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Agibot: An Open-Source Modular Swerve-Drive Robot Platform for Agricultural Robotics Research and Education
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Agricultural production faces persistent labor shortages and increasing demand for automation, yet progress in agricultural robotics remains constrained by the limited availability of affordable, flexible, and accessible research platforms. This paper presents Agibot, an open-source, modular, low-cost agricultural robotics platform designed for autonomy research and experimentation, with potential applications in hands-on robotics education. The platform integrates four-wheel independent swerve drive, swappable computing, distributed embedded control, multimodal sensing, and configurable manipulation within a unified sense-plan-act-verify framework supporting perception, control, navigation, manipulation, and autonomous task verification. The platform was evaluated through representative row-crop navigation and manipulation tasks under varying lighting and soil conditions. Experiments demonstrated reliable lane following, autonomous row-to-row navigation, target identification, seed dispensing, plant manipulation, and closed-loop verification of task success. Its modular architecture supports independent testing, modification, and validation of autonomy components for rapid prototyping and experimentation. These proof-of-concept tasks, controller-tuning studies, and integrated trials demonstrate the platform's research capabilities, while its accessible and reconfigurable design supports its use for hands-on robotics education. By combining affordability, modularity, open-source accessibility, configurable manipulation, and end-to-end sense-plan-act-verify autonomy, Agibot provides a practical platform for agricultural robotics research, technology development, and workforce training.
Systems and Control (EESS).comment: 14 pages. Submitted to IEEE Transactions on AgriFood Electronics (TAFE)

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Sample-Covariance Regularization for Data-Driven Predictive Control from Frequency Response Functions under Colored Noise
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: In this work, we investigate how sample covariance obtained from frequency-response functions (FRFs) can be exploited to improve performance of data-driven frequency-domain predictive control (FreePC) in the presence of colored measurement noise. In case of periodic multisine excitation, this covariance is obtained directly from repeated periods and provides a frequency-dependent measure of uncertainty without requiring an additional parametric noise model. To incorporate this information into both indirect and direct predictive control, we develop a frequency-domain subspace predictive controller (FD-SPC) and establish its equivalence to the direct FreePC formulation in the noiseless setting. Regularization terms for both formulations are then motivated by expected prediction-error criteria and constructed from the sample covariance of the FRF estimates. Across all tested noise models and data sizes, regularization consistently reduces the median realized control cost relative to the corresponding controller without covariance regularization, with reductions of up to 35%.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Conformalized Data-Driven Reachability Analysis with PAC Guarantees
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Data-driven reachability analysis computes reachable sets directly from noisy data. Existing matrix-zonotope reachability methods require a known noise bound, and their nonlinear extensions require a Lipschitz constant. We propose Conformalized Data-Driven Reachability, which calibrates the open-loop prediction error of a least-squares model with training-conditional split conformal prediction and propagates the initial set and the input set with zonotopes. The resulting sets contain the whole trajectory with a probably approximately correct (PAC) guarantee that requires only independent and identically distributed trajectories, and the number of calibration trajectories does not depend on the horizon. The prediction error depends on the initial states and the controller only through the model error. The method extends to measurement noise with a known quantile and to nonlinear systems through local affine models. In experiments, the sets keep an average coverage above 99% when the initial states and the controller change, whereas sets calibrated directly on the states lose coverage.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Control of Linear Dynamical Systems with Operational Constraints
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: This paper presents a method for designing servo-controllers that enforce operational constraints on multi-input multi-output linear time-invariant dynamical systems. The proposed method introduces a control augmentation that complements a baseline controller to ensure forward invariance of state/output trajectories within prescribed box constraints. The derivations of the control design are based on the Nagumo Theorem, the Comparison Lemma, and principles from min-norm optimal control akin to the theory of Control Barrier Functions. Importantly, an explicit piecewise-linear feedback control law is derived, which provides continuous enforcement of constraints without online optimization, enabling rigorous stability and robustness analysis via classical linear systems theory. Extensions to handle estimation errors in output feedback and integral action in proportional-integral control are provided. Theoretical results are validated through flight control simulation studies that demonstrate input/output constraint satisfaction, robustness to disturbances, and closed-loop stability. The proposed method offers a mathematically rigorous, practical, and analyzable alternative to common heuristic or optimization-intensive constrained control strategies.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Open-Source Multi-Fidelity EMT Modeling of Data Center Loads for Power System Studies
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Characterizing data center-grid interactions under rapid load fluctuations requires electromagnetic transient (EMT) models that capture fast converter and control dynamics. This paper develops a modular multi-fidelity EMT model of data center loads in PSCAD. The modular design supports flexible assembly of subsystem models for different power supply configurations. The multi-fidelity design incorporates switching models, average-converter models, and reduced-order models to balance simulation accuracy and computational efficiency according to analysis needs. The model also provides a systematic controller tuning procedure and supports control mode switching. Comparative simulations demonstrate how this data center load model responds to both grid-side and load-side disturbances and assess the accuracy and computational efficiency of models with three fidelity levels. The model is publicly available on GitHub.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Quantum Natural Muon: Spectral-Natural Optimization for Variational Quantum Circuits
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Training parameterized quantum circuits requires optimization methods that account for two distinct structures: the information geometry of quantum states and the matrix or tensor structure induced by circuit parameterization. We introduce Quantum Natural Muon (QNM), a spectral natural-gradient framework that applies polar normalization to circuit-semantic parameter blocks after damped quantum Fisher preconditioning. This ordering is essential: quantum Fisher preconditioning and blockwise polar normalization do not commute in general, so QNM is not an order-free composition of quantum natural gradient (QNG) and Muon. We show that Frobenius-matched polar mixing preserves active singular subspaces while raising a spectral floor and improving active conditioning, and that the resulting direction remains a controlled perturbation of QNG. For its distance-aware realization (DA-QNM), we further establish alignment, descent, and nonconvex stationarity guarantees for the normalized update, together with perturbation bounds under gradient and QFIM estimation error. Experiments on variational quantum eigensolving, weighted QAOA-MaxCut, and supervised quantum classification isolate the roles of quantum geometry, circuit-semantic spectral structure, and radius control. The strongest gains arise when the spectral blocks match the circuit structure, supporting the central principle that quantum-state and structured spectral geometries provide complementary information for variational quantum optimization.

Robotics.title: World In-Context Learning for Agentic Robot Manipulation
Robotics.summary: Trained action policies write manipulation skill into network weights, tying what is learned to the distribution it is learned from. In-context learning (ICL) avoids this coupling but has not matched trained policies, because a demonstration recorded in another scene carries no feedback from the world the robot currently faces. We observe that what an agent learns in context is semantic, recording task steps and object roles rather than visual appearance, so experience gathered in one world transfers to another. Based on this insight, we propose World In-Context Learning (WICL), a paradigm in which a frozen model starts from a demonstration, rehearses the task in a world such as a simulator, and writes the feedback into its context rather than its weights. We build RoboScript, a modular infrastructure that implements WICL for agentic manipulation. From a single demonstration, RoboScript learns each task through rehearsal in simulation, freezes the learned knowledge as a Task Memory, and deploys the frozen memory on new scenes with data isolation that ensures every deployment input is available on a real robot. On all 50 tasks of RoboTwin 2.0, RoboScript reaches 83.4% mean success across clean and randomized settings with one demonstration per task and no gradient updates, exceeding the strongest trained action policy by over 20 points. The method generalizes across visual distributions, improves through reflection, scales with the foundation model, and transfers to a physical dual-arm robot through cross-embodiment memory adaptation. With a world in the loop, a robot can learn a manipulation task in its context as well as it learns one in its weights. All code is available at https://github.com/ArcheOne-AI/RoboScript

Robotics.title: SWAM: Scaling World Action Models with Cross-Modal Alignment
Robotics.summary: World action models jointly predict video and actions conditioned on language. Existing studies focus primarily on architectures and training mechanisms, typically treating language-video alignment acquired through video pretraining as an established foundation. However, introducing action learning may impair this alignment. Principled guidance on data and supervision design for maintaining language-video alignment during action learning remains limited. To investigate this, we curate a pool of approximately 47,000 hours of general videos, egocentric videos, UMI demonstrations, and robot demonstrations. Building on this, we systematically study how language-video supervision, language-video-action supervision, and the joint use of these two forms affect WAM performance. In particular, we examine how language annotation quality affects pretrained language-video capabilities, and how action supervision from UMI and robot demonstrations extends these capabilities to language-video-action modeling. To better scale the model, we further conduct detailed studies on joint training recipe and model architecture. Under a fixed training budget, mixing egocentric videos and UMI demonstrations improves control generalization. Model architecture affects how effectively these experiences are used, while scaling pretraining under the selected configuration brings further gains. The resulting recipe, post-trained on RoboTwin Clean demonstrations only, achieves success rates of 88.10% and 61.56% under Easy (Clean-to-Clean) and Hard (Clean-to-Random) conditions, respectively. Our model achieves 40.00% SR across three real-world tasks, compared with 23.33% for the strongest baseline, indicating better generalization under unseen conditions. We release the curated data, training code, and model weights.

Robotics.title: Integrated hybrid edge-cloud architecture for multi-robot and human-robot collaboration using ROS 2-MQTT-FIWARE in Mediterranean Greenhouses
Robotics.summary: The imperative to develop more sustainable agriculture demands a transition from isolated automation toward the deployment of multi-robot systems (MRS) in agrifood environments. However, Mediterranean greenhouse settings-characterized by narrow corridors, dense biomass, and structural metallic interference-pose significant challenges for robust and scalable communication between agents. Traditional robotic frameworks, such as ROS 2, frequently encounter node discovery issues and latency spikes due to dynamic obstacles, dense foliage, and other characteristic greenhouse elements, creating a critical bottleneck for real-time coordination. This paper proposes an innovative cloud-based hybrid architecture that establishes a two-way communication bridge between ROS 2, acting as an edge computing platform, and iVeg as a Decision Support System (DSS), using MQTT and the European FIWARE platform. The proposed framework enables seamless interoperability between fleets of multiple robots in environments with communication constraints, facilitating the synchronised exchange of high-level telemetry, point cloud data and farmer identification for collaboration, amongst other critical data. The architecture was validated in a high-fidelity simulation environment and subsequently tested in a real-world greenhouse scenario, demonstrating its ability to maintain persistent connectivity and data integrity under adverse network conditions. The results indicate that the integration of MQTT effectively eliminates information silos, providing a scalable and decentralised solution for managing complex robotic missions, which are executed locally via Edge Computing. This work sets a new methodological precedent for the concept of Greenhouse Models as a Service (GMaaS), bridging the gap between low-level robotic control and high-level, cloud-based IoT decision-making.

Robotics.title: An offline approach to fNIRS-guided reinforcement learning for robot behavior
Robotics.summary: Human-in-the-loop Reinforcement Learning has become a popular approach for training, finetuning, and aligning robot behavior with user preferences. Our paper explores the feasibility of using brain signals via functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) to modulate robot learning in simulation. We compare agents trained on passive (observational) versus active (demonstrative) interaction tasks, and test multiple methods for enhancing the RL algorithm with the neural signal, focusing on parameter augmentation in contrast to replacement. We further examine how model granularity and noise affect agent learning. Our results show that this framework is effective. The neural signal improves learning when augmenting trajectory priorities and state-action q-targets. Additionally, the framework learns successfully from offline data, offering a practical alternative for settings where real-time BCI setups are impractical or only limited data is available.
Robotics.comment: Accepted at the 4th Workshop on Nonverbal Cues for Human-Robot Cooperative Intelligence (IROS 2026). 5 pages, 3 figures

Robotics.title: DreamLander: A 6-DOF World Model based Reinforcement Learning Planetary Lander
Robotics.summary: Soft powered descent landings are becoming evermore important in the field of space exploration and scientific advancement, because of their ability to deliver mission critical payloads, both highly accurately and safely. The high efficiency restriction on planetary landings due to the severely limited fuel supply results in the need for optimal guidance trajectories and control. Model based reinforcement learning is proving to be an important tool in simplifying the highly complex process of generating optimal guidance trajectories and control. In this work, we present DreamLander, a state of the art model based reinforcement learning algorithm based on DreamerV3, to generate optimal guidance and control for a realistic 6 degree of freedom entry descent landing problem. The model based approach creates a sample efficient and highly generalizable model that can be applied to a variety of scenarios whilst maintaining a high degree of accuracy, landing within 2 meters of the designated landing zone, and with velocity norm less than 0.3 meters per second. DreamLander makes use of state sensor observations, making progress toward End-to-End solutions of the Entry Descent Landing problem.

Robotics.title: Simulating Vein Compressibility for Ultrasound-Guided Femoral Access: Speed, Accuracy, and Phantom Validation
Robotics.summary: In ultrasound-guided femoral access, probe pressure deforms the tissue and changes the vascular anatomy a robot observes. A simulator must reproduce these mechanics fast enough for robotic interaction, yet the computational effort needed for a clinically meaningful signal like vein collapse before artery is unclear. We test the feasibility of a physics-based simulation in NVIDIA's Isaac Sim for Healthcare, with Stable Neo-Hookean tissue solved by Vertex Block Descent on one GPU. A simulation of a low-fidelity cylindrical benchtop phantom with known geometry and mechanical properties, pressed by a robot, predicted its artery within 5 percentage points at every depth. It matched the vein within 3 points through 11 mm of a 25.4 mm press and followed the collapse behavior of the low-fidelity physical phantom. Across element size, time step, and solver iterations, wall clock time per frame scaled linearly with solver work, but accuracy did not improve with more work. The chosen setting reduced solver time per frame by a factor of 976, from 29,700 ms to 30.4 ms, while remaining within 1.03 points of the finest reference setting. The physics solver alone took 30.4 ms per frame, while the full stack, including ultrasound and graphics rendering, took 56.4 ms per frame. Finally, when seeded with realistic literature-based mechanical properties, the digital leg model compressed the vein far more than the artery at every setting, reproducing the expected clinical signal of vein collapse before artery, which is used to distinguish them. In total, these results suggest that the NVIDIA Isaac Sim platform may be suitable for augmenting reinforcement learning training or online simulation for autonomous femoral access with ultrasound.
Robotics.comment: Submitted to the Journal of Medical Robotics Research (JMRR) for the International Symposium of Medical Robotics 2027 (ISMR 2027) 11 Pages (8 main + 3 references), 4 figures in main body

Robotics.title: Learning Heterogeneous Tactile Representation for General Dexterous Manipulation
Robotics.summary: Tactile sensing is an indispensable modality for contact-rich dexterous manipulation, a capability that hints at the ultimate frontiers of embodied intelligence. However, commercially available tactile sensors are still at a relatively early stage of development, with each type of sensor offering irreplaceable strengths alongside its own drawbacks. A key challenge is thus to free tactile understanding from sensor-specific physics, so that embodied models can effectively leverage heterogeneous tactile data. To this end, we develop LingBot-Touch, a tactile foundation model characterized by the following properties. (i) Our model yields a unified representation across different tactile sensors (i.e., piezoresistive, magnetic, and visuotactile sensors), and is easily extensible to new sensor types. (ii) The resulting tactile tokens are plug-and-play: they can be seamlessly integrated into policy models across paradigms, from diffusion policy to vision-language-action (VLA) models such as $π_{0.5}$ and LingBot-VLA, consistently enhancing manipulation dexterity. (iii) Extensive experiments, spanning simulation and real-robot deployments across multiple hardware platforms, demonstrate that our tactile representation substantially benefits complex manipulation tasks while maintaining strong computational efficiency. We believe the findings in this work demonstrate the potential of leveraging cross-sensor data to scale tactile learning, and offer encouraging insights for the design of future hardware and embodied models.

Robotics.title: Benchmarking Real-World Robotic Manipulation through Stochastic Challenges
Robotics.summary: A challenging bottleneck in manipulation research is reproducibility and comparability of methods in real-world environments. Since manipulation is an interactive task, it cannot be evaluated on a static dataset of observations. Benchmarking in simulation is a common remedy, but cannot cover the whole complexity of real-world tests. This paper proposes a new paradigm of stochastic challenges. Like the well-known YCB objects, it is based on reproducible real-world scenes and therefore allows system-level innovation and comparability between different platforms. Due to their stochastic nature, our challenges however, mimic the rigor and surprise of hidden test sets. To this end, we show how different robots in different labs can be compared based on their success rate over different random task samples, if these samples come from the same distribution. We propose stochastic challenges as a general paradigm for robot benchmarking and implement this paradigm in a novel benchmark for mobile manipulation, on which we compare two robots tested in two different labs.
Robotics.comment: Accepted at the 10th Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL 2026). 15 pages, 3 figures

Robotics.title: Certified Zonotopic Reachability Analysis for Trajectory Tracking on Lie Groups
Robotics.summary: Autonomous vehicles track planned trajectories close to obstacles. Unknown disturbances make them deviate from these trajectories. With a bound on the tracking error that disturbances can cause, a planned trajectory can be certified as safe before execution. Existing set-based methods bound the tracking error by one invariant ellipsoid for the whole trajectory or by intervals, which are both conservative. For aerial and space vehicles, the tracking error evolves on a matrix Lie group with nonlinear dynamics. However, for group-affine systems, the error dynamics are linear in Lie algebra coordinates when the vehicle receives the inputs of the reference. The control input and the disturbance enter through the inverse right Jacobian, a matrix that depends on the error. We propagate the linear part of the error dynamics with zonotopes and enclose the effect of the inverse right Jacobian on the disturbance in closed form. The resulting tubes are tight and provably contain all reachable tracking errors in continuous time. When some error components have no input, the inverse right Jacobian leaves unmatched nonlinear terms in the closed loop. None of the tested methods certifies such a closed loop. Hybrid coordinates make these terms matched, so that our controller cancels every nonlinear term that does not contain the disturbance. Our tubes give tighter bounds than the ellipsoid method in simulations of a planar aircraft and a fully actuated multirotor and in real flights of a quadrotor, where the tube contains every measured attitude error. Under larger disturbances and the same feedback gain, the ellipsoid method yields no valid ellipsoid, whereas our tubes remain valid.

Robotics.title: Sliding into Balance: Benefits of a Sliding Payload for Load Distribution and Disturbance Rejection in Dual-UAV Transportation
Robotics.summary: This paper analyzes the cooperative transportation of a payload suspended from two drones in which, instead of being attached to two independent ropes, the payload is allowed to slide along a single rope connecting both UAVs. First, a planar nondimensional dynamical model of the sliding motion with viscous friction is presented. Then, considering stationary drones, this configuration is compared with a fixed payload with the same total rope length, both at equilibrium and under disturbances. The analytical results show that the sliding payload equalizes the tension in both rope segments for any relative position of the drones, so that no rope loses tension at equilibrium; it doubles the region reachable by the payload and, except for low friction combined with a large drone separation, it enlarges the set of admissible disturbances. Finally, a dynamic simulation also shows that under realistic gusty wind profiles, the average tension imbalance between the drones is reduced with respect to the fixed-payload solution.

Robotics.title: $Σ$-LeWM: Learning World Models via S-Information for Robot Control
Robotics.summary: World models have increasingly been applied as a model-based control method for robotics tasks such as manipulation and locomotion. While early world model architectures relied on decoders to prevent mode collapse and learn a predictable latent space, recent works on world models, such as Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture or LeWorldModel, increasingly aim to learn embeddings without a grounding decoder, utilising only a latent forward dynamics predictor and a stabilising entropy term. In this paper, we set out to demonstrate that the further introduction of two additional latent losses to LeWorldModel, a backward dynamics predictor and an inverse dynamics action predictor, enforces further structure on the latent embedding, leading to further gains in both performance and planning efficiency. These are critical properties for improving the applicability of such methods to real-time model-based control of real-world robots.
