Robotics.summary: Vision-based rover autonomy requires integrating perception, localization, planning and platform-specific control under limited sensing and computing resources. We present an open-source ROS 2 stack for following directional arrows, reaching a terminal cone and returning autonomously to the start. It connects YOLOv8n detection and geometric direction, range and bearing estimation with RGB-D SLAM, wheel-inertial state estimation, kinematics-aware planning, behavior-tree mission management and STM32 actuation. Standard interfaces separate reusable autonomy from the hardware layer; a proportional path-following plugin supports low-speed rover motion. Public resources include software, configuration, a labeled dataset, trained weights and evaluation logs. On 478 held-out images, the detector achieves mAP@0.5 of 0.720 under the Ultralytics evaluator and outperforms a classical OpenCV baseline under a shared evaluation protocol. The reported perception latency is 25 ms on a Jetson Orin NX. Three missions, one indoor and two outdoor, demonstrate marker-guided navigation and autonomous return without operator motion commands or reported collisions. Field results document integration failures and corrective choices; repeated instrumented trials remain necessary to quantify physical navigation errors and reliability.

Robotics.title: Ground Reaction Force-Aware Model Predictive Control for Underactuated Upright Physical Assistance
Robotics.summary: Many rehabilitation robots execute prescribed motions using reactive tracking controllers that do not explicitly incorporate the user's instantaneous human-ground interaction. This paper presents Ground Reaction Force-Aware Model Predictive Control (GRF-MPC), a framework for upright physical assistance. By integrating live GRF and center of pressure (CoP) measurements directly into a human centroidal dynamics model, GRF-MPC formulates a real-time quadratic program (QP) that optimizes assistive forces and moments over a receding horizon. We deployed GRF-MPC on the Robotic Upright Stand Trainer (RobUST) in an underactuated 4-cable configuration and evaluated it against a fully actuated 8-cable Cartesian impedance baseline in nearly 300 trials across six healthy participants. Across tasks spanning impulsive perturbations, lunge trajectories, and voluntary limits of stability, GRF-MPC reduced peak planar center-of-mass (CoM) error by 19.6% during perturbations, lowered trajectory tracking error by 24.1%, required 28.7% less net mechanical work, and permitted a 45.9% greater normalized voluntary excursion area. The underlying QP solves in under 1 ms, comfortably enabling 100 Hz replanning and demonstrating that incorporating live human-ground interaction into predictive control yields stronger, more transparent physical assistance with half the actuators.
Robotics.comment: Accepted for publication in IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (RA-L), October 2026. 8 pages, 5 figures

Robotics.title: How Much of Your VLA Is kNN
Robotics.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models now exceed 95% success on the LIBERO simulation benchmark, yet it remains unclear how much of this performance requires generalization beyond the training demonstrations. In this work, we show that retrieving nearby demonstrations and reusing their action chunks achieves a success rate of 91.7 % on LIBERO without policy training. Under LIBERO-Plus perturbations, retrieval shows the smallest drop of all evaluated policies. Across nine publicly available VLAs, fine-tuning mostly makes the vision-language backbone a better retrieval key, and the actions of the VLAs remain close to the demonstrations. In addition, we introduce Local Action Consistency (LAC), an offline metric that measures whether nearby observations in representation space are also associated with similar future actions. We show that LAC tracks the success rate of retrieval and can guide the training of a retrieval key. Our evaluation and source code are available at https://github.com/sereact/lerobot_knn.
Robotics.comment: 21 pages, 10 figures, accepted to the CoRL 2026 G2A/TAG workshop

Robotics.title: Show, Don't Tell: Detecting Novel Objects by Watching Human Videos
Robotics.summary: How can a robot quickly identify and recognize new objects shown to it during a human demonstration? Existing closed-set object detectors frequently fail at this because the objects are out-of-distribution. While open-set detectors (e.g., VLMs) sometimes succeed, they often require expensive and tedious human-in-the-loop prompt engineering to uniquely recognize novel object instances. In this paper, we present a self-supervised system that eliminates the need for tedious language descriptions and expensive prompt engineering by training a bespoke object detector on an automatically created dataset, supervised by the human demonstration itself. In our approach, "Show, Don't Tell," we show the detector the specific objects of interest during the demonstration, rather than telling the detector about these objects via complex language descriptions. By bypassing language altogether, this paradigm enables us to quickly train bespoke detectors tailored to the relevant objects observed in human task demonstrations. We develop an integrated on-robot system to deploy our "Show, Don't Tell" paradigm of automatic dataset creation and novel object-detection on a real-world robot. Empirical results demonstrate that our pipeline significantly outperforms state-of-the-art detection and recognition methods for manipulated objects, leading to improved task completion for the robot.

Robotics.title: DOBB: Dynamic Oriented Bounding Boxes for Multi-Agent Collision Avoidance under State Uncertainty and Heterogeneous Dynamics
Robotics.summary: Learning-based decentralized collision avoidance must remain reliable under state-estimation uncertainty and heterogeneous agent dynamics. Existing methods typically address these factors through training-domain variation or by exposing uncertainty and capability estimates to the policy at runtime. However, both leave the policy to infer how these quantities should alter the physical separation required for safe interaction, which can couple collision-avoidance behavior to relationships learned from the training distribution. We introduce the Dynamic Oriented Bounding Box (DOBB), an online geometric representation that maps the current state estimate, uncertainty, and agent-specific response characteristics into a dynamic, direction-dependent safety margin. We derive geometric features that jointly characterize the relative configuration and severity of interactions between agents' DOBBs, along with a reward function that preserves the physical interpretation of those interactions. Across four evaluation environments, DOBB achieves the lowest mean total failure rate of 2.6%. This performance persists under out-of-distribution shifts in actuation dynamics and state-estimation uncertainty, with collision-based failure remaining at or below 2.3% in every tested condition. We attribute this robustness to the geometric abstraction of the safety margin, which is less coupled to the specific uncertainty and actuation regimes encountered during training.

Robotics.title: ASPIRE: An Agentic System-Identification Platform for Iterative Reasoning and Exploration
Robotics.summary: System identification requires expert decisions on the identification method, incorporation of prior physical knowledge, and model validation. We propose ASPIRE, a framework for nonlinear system identification in which a large language model agent selects and executes the identification method. ASPIRE constructs closed-form, nonlinear static or dynamic models from measured data, optionally supplemented by a system description, the intended use of the model, and physical requirements expressed formally or in natural language. Each model includes its parameters, an estimation record, an interpretation of its terms, and an error evaluated on test data inaccessible to the agent. Formal physical requirements are verified independently. ASPIRE operates autonomously or interactively, allowing the agent to ask questions and the user to request further analyses and identification rounds. We evaluate ASPIRE on three measured systems: a mobile robot, a rotational system with dry friction, and a laboratory fermenter. Each system is tested with and without a description, in five runs per task. All 30 runs delivered valid models, at a cost of 0.96 to 3.38 US dollars per run. An assessment by the authors found that, for the 30 models recommended by the agent, one per run, the interpretation of the model and the documentation of its structure selection and parameter estimation fully satisfied 132 of 150 assessed items and partly satisfied 18. The most frequent discrepancy, found in nine models, concerned inaccurate or unsupported claims about model structure selection.

Robotics.title: Robo-MLT: Dual-System Robotic Manipulation for Long-Horizon Medical Laboratory Tasks
Robotics.summary: Reliable medical laboratory automation requires robots to complete entire workflows in protocol order while handling changes during execution. A robot may execute each motion correctly yet fail the workflow by confusing visually similar stages or stalling after human intervention. We present Robo-MLT, a dual-system framework that couples explicit workflow monitoring with learned action generation. A vision--language planner composes an ordered atomic-skill sequence from the protocol and the initial workspace observation. A multiframe execution monitor detects when the active skill has completed or become infeasible, then advances the workflow or triggers replanning. A skill-conditioned vision--language--action policy generates the manipulation trajectories, and an asynchronous runtime coordinates it with the monitor. We evaluate Robo-MLT against four policy baselines and a VLM-based monitor baseline on blood gas analysis and blood sample tube sorting, with 50 nominal configurations per method and 20 sample-removal configurations. Robo-MLT achieves task success rates of 82\% and 70\%, exceeding $π_{0.5}$ by 30 and 22 percentage points, respectively. After an operator removes the sample being handled, the system revises the remaining plan and continues processing the other samples. These results indicate that, under the evaluated conditions, explicit workflow monitoring makes long-horizon laboratory manipulation more reliable and recoverable.

Robotics.title: RoboACE: Adversarial Co-Evolution for Robot Self-Improvement
Robotics.summary: Robot agents can improve reusable skills, planning procedures, and recovery strategies from execution feedback, yet a fixed practice source leaves the search for new weaknesses unchanged. Useful practice depends on the agent's current capabilities, so the procedure that chooses practice must also be revisable. We present RoboACE (Robot Adversarial Co-Evolution), a framework that jointly evolves curriculum and execution harnesses around frozen foundation models. The curriculum harness uses accumulated capability evidence to propose informative challenges, while the execution harness responds with reusable revisions that expand execution capabilities. Alternating updates hold one side fixed as the other changes, and admitted challenges form fixed snapshots for comparing execution revisions. Starting from a compact set of LIBERO practice conditions, the resulting frozen deployment outperforms the evaluated controllers and agent systems across four LIBERO-family panels. On LIBERO-PRO, it reaches 74.0% success, exceeding the initial deployment by 15.0 percentage points and direct execution by its VLA controller by 13.5 points. Case studies document changes to evidence-guided practice selection, drawer-skill grounding, and controller intervention.

Multiagent Systems.title: Bench-MFG: A Benchmark Suite for Learning in Stationary Mean Field Games
Multiagent Systems.summary: The rise of Mean Field Games (MFGs) has fostered a growing family of algorithms designed to solve large-scale multi-agent systems. However, the field currently lacks a standardized evaluation protocol, forcing researchers to rely on bespoke, isolated, and often simplistic environments. This fragmentation makes it difficult to assess the robustness, generalization, and failure modes of emerging methods. To address this gap, we propose a comprehensive benchmark suite for MFGs, focusing on the discrete-time, discrete-space, stationary setting. We introduce a taxonomy of problem classes, ranging from no-interaction and monotone games to potential and dynamics-coupled games, and provide prototypical environments for each. Furthermore, we present MF-Garnets, a method for generating random MFG instances to facilitate rigorous statistical testing. We benchmark a variety of learning algorithms across these environments, including a novel population-based approach (MF-PSO). To our knowledge, this is the first benchmark for MFGs.

Multiagent Systems.title: Modelling Opinion Dynamics at Scale with Deep MARL
Multiagent Systems.summary: Modelling opinion dynamics typically relies on hand-crafted local interaction rules to study emergent macroscopic phenomena such as consensus and polarisation. In contrast, multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) enables agents to learn such behaviours directly by optimising simple rewards. To explore the potential of MARL for opinion dynamics, we introduce a GPU-accelerated consensus and truth-finding game that scales to populations of up to 1000 agents, comparable to many real-world social sub-networks. To prevent unrealistic conventions, we extend other-play to general-sum social interactions. We next validate our model on a subset of the Bluesky network by recovering agent importance structures from graph topology alone via a learned attention layer, finding that highly conforming populations most closely match human data. In large social media networks, such high levels of conformity significantly reduce collective accuracy and promote dishonest agents that lie to fit in. By contrast, small hunter-gatherer networks are less affected; here, conformity can even improve collective agreement. This suggests a mismatch between evolved human conformity heuristics and modern social media environments as a potential contributor to misinformation.
Multiagent Systems.comment: 39 pages, 31 figures. Accepted at the 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026)

Multiagent Systems.title: Multi-Agent Screening: What Agreement and Acceptance Cannot Tell You
Multiagent Systems.summary: When AI agents screen items for a costly human assessor, as in agentic search, e-discovery and AI reviewing of papers, only what they pass gets judged. We show what each kind of evidence can establish about their errors, even with unlimited data. Agreement shows that agents concur, not that they are right, however many there are. Acceptance by the assessor gives precision but only a lower bound on recall. Knowing which agents found which relevant items gives an upper bound on recall if agents' finds are not negatively correlated, and caps what one more agent can add if agents are interchangeable. Without assumptions about the agents, recall can be pinned down only by judging items they did not pass: a random sample of these estimates how many relevant items were missed, to any chosen accuracy, and the sample needed does not grow with the number of agents.

Multiagent Systems.title: Teamknitt: Configuring, Observing and Intervening in LLM-Agent Teams through the Lens of Dynamical-Systems and Human-Team Theory
Multiagent Systems.summary:
Most frameworks for teams of large language model (LLM) agents fix the team's shape inside the software: who talks to whom, how much is passed along, and what a human can do once a run has started. Human-team research has long asked those questions: where team phenomena live (in members or in their interaction), how team-level properties arise, and what separates what a team does from how a team is. I propose using that theory as the organizing lens for configuring, observing and intervening in LLM-agent teams, without assuming its findings transfer.
  I introduce teamknitt, a framework and open reference implementation in which a user configures a team of 1-16 AI agents for task completion, solution generation, achieving a goal or a research mission; selects one of fourteen deterministic routing topologies or a custom directed graph; chooses a sharing profile that limits what may travel along permitted routes; and binds sources, representations, work dependencies, handoffs and an expertise directory. The recorded process can be observed through non-system views (member reports and behavior) and system views (distributed problem-solving, differentiated transactive memory, interactive coordination, team dynamics). Interventions are explicit and human-led: reviewed reconfiguration between runs, planned disturbances, and private feedback, pause, resume or stop applied at dependency-wave boundaries, with "queued", "applied", "assembled", "understood" and "improved" kept as separate claims. Emergent states such as trust and shared understanding are declared unmeasured.
  This is an idea and system-description paper with falsifiable hypotheses on topology, information flow and intervention timing, including whether the fractal scaling of communication output between members, and between members on different models, relates to task and team performance. No comparative result is reported.
Multiagent Systems.comment: 17 pages, 3 figures, 6 tables. Reference implementation v0.9.0: https://github.com/JeranRolevs/teamknitt

Multiagent Systems.title: Rate-Aware Quantum-Inspired Trajectory Learning for Interference-Limited Multi-UAV Networks
Multiagent Systems.summary: Placing unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) as aerial base stations is non-convex and combinatorial, so practical methods first discretize the continuous airspace into a finite set of candidate positions---a uniform grid or clustering centroids---and optimize over that set. Built from Euclidean distance alone, the candidate set is channel-blind: it ignores line-of-sight probability and the co-channel interference that limits achievable rate under full frequency reuse. No optimizer can select a position the candidate set omits, so good locations the geometry missed are lost before the search begins. We propose Rate-Aware Quantum-Assisted Graph Condensation (RA-QAGC), a two-stage framework that makes the candidate set itself the object of optimization. The first stage constructs it by annealing a cost that embeds tier-weighted achievable rate, mean co-channel interference, and an explicit minimum-rate penalty, yielding a compact, mobility-feasible waypoint graph. The second stage learns trajectories over that graph with decentralized independent Q-learning agents, replacing a centralized joint-action table with one compact table per UAV. RA-QAGC improves priority-tier throughput by 21--54\% over seven baselines, including recent graph-neural and deep Q-network schemes, at no significant cost in aggregate throughput, and the margin widens as the fleet densifies. We additionally examine the quantum-inspired acceptance rule that recent aerial-networking work advocates, and report that its tunnelling floor confers no measurable advantage over classical simulated annealing at any fleet size tested, while annealing itself clearly outperforms greedy and random placement.

Multiagent Systems.title: Unprompted coordination through shared memory in LLM agents: a locked two-implementation replication and extension
Multiagent Systems.summary: Coordination between large language-model agents has become a central question for AI safety and software engineering, as such agents are deployed in groups that share infrastructure. Existing research tells the agents that partners exist or asks them to coordinate. Whether coordination arises through shared state alone, with nothing disclosing that anyone else is present, is the key question for deployments that share caches and memory between agents, yet it has rarely been examined, and never with independent replication; this study does both. Four agents each received a short arithmetic task and a key-value store presented to each as its own scratch space; two held complementary halves of one computation, and no prompt mentioned other agents, sharing or collaboration. For reliability, the environment was rebuilt independently from a written protocol, and both implementations ran under hashed locks on design, data and analysis. The results bear novelty value in three respects. Joint success occurred only through the shared store. Whether a model coordinated depended not on its vendor tier but on whether it wrote its intermediate result and looked at the store again, and one ordinary sentence, "check your workspace again before submitting", switched that second look on and off. The findings held under replication. For practice, state shared between agents is a communication channel and should be separated, namespaced and logged. For research, designs should be locked before the data, and the parse rule, endpoint and parameters reported. Future work should test open-weight models and separate using another agent's output from intending to communicate.
Multiagent Systems.comment: 13 pages, 7 tables, 2 figures. Replication package: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23965306

Multiagent Systems.title: A Modular Perspective for Modeling MARL Systems
Multiagent Systems.summary:
The growing complexity of Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) has fragmented the literature, obscuring underlying architectural choices behind diverse implementations. This fragmentation makes it difficult to evaluate critical modeling dimensions in isolation, identify how components affect the resulting system dynamics, and compare, reuse, or combine contributions across the literature.
  This paper proposes a modular perspective for modeling, analyzing, and implementing MARL systems. We decompose them into eight functional modules: agents, environments, learning, reward modeling, training and execution modes, communication, modeling of other agents, and evaluation criteria. For each module, we clarify its role and review representative approaches.
  We instantiate this decomposition in MARLKIT, a framework whose modules are explicit and interchangeable. MARLKIT demonstrates how the proposed perspective supports transparent experimental assumptions and the controlled variation and combination of MARL mechanisms. Experiments illustrate its ability to prototype, compare, reuse and combine modules while making differences between configurations explicit.
  Overall, the paper provides a structured perspective on MARL modeling and implementation, offering a common language for making modeling choices explicit, supporting clearer descriptions of MARL approaches, and supporting more controlled experimentation through the systematic isolation and combination of MARL mechanisms.

Multiagent Systems.title: Modelling socio-economic effects of the pandemic in a metropolitan area
Multiagent Systems.summary: One of the most notorious measures taken by authorities in every country trying to prevent the uncontrollable spread of the Covid 19 pandemic was to impose severe measures to diminish the mobility of people. In recent publications we proposed a mathematical model to address the consequences of these measures and to predict the infections under different scenarios, for various different countries. In this paper we extend the model, called the BTH--SEIRS-model, to deal with the reduction of mobility in an urban area. The chosen region was the densely-populated metropolitan area around Helsinki, the capital of Finland. This choice obeyed to the fact that there are precise data related to mobility from a mobile telephone company, and that this region was completely isolated from the rest of the country for a short period during the pandemic. We also used public transport data from railways and the accommodation occupation rates in the area of interest. We show that the BTH--SEIRS model is capable of simulating the real infection data as well as the mobility-related economic activity, exhibiting the main trends present in the three indicators used for comparison. Our calculations allow us to highlight the difference of the behaviour of the pandemic in a totally different spatial scale, and to discover the hidden factors that govern the behaviour of people who are forced to commute every day from home to work.

Multiagent Systems.title: Agent4Crypto: A Dual-Reflective and Market-Feedback-Aligned LLM-Based Multi-Agent System for Cryptocurrency Trading
Multiagent Systems.summary: Cryptocurrency markets provide a natural testbed for autonomous AI agents because they are digital-native, high-frequency, and machine-speed environments, yet existing methods often struggle with non-stationary market regimes, opaque decisions, and fixed aggregation rules. In this paper, we propose Agent4Crypto, a dual-reflective and market-feedback-aligned multi-agent system. The framework coordinates specialized agents for data collection, analysis, risk assessment, reflection, and trading, synthesizing heterogeneous signals from prices, indicators, news, and charts in an interpretable decision pipeline. Our central design is a trader-centric decision mechanism: three style-specific trader agents, Aggressive, Neutral, and Conservative, generate candidate actions and natural-language rationales from the same market context, while their influence is learned rather than manually fixed. A PPO-based gating policy dynamically allocates trader weights through a dual-reflective feedback process. One reflection stream evaluates post-trade decision quality from realized portfolio outcomes and distills reusable lessons into a Financial ReasoningBank for retrieval in subsequent trader prompts, while the other estimates trader-level counterfactual contribution, indicating which style has recently aligned better with market movements. The PPO state combines Counterfactual Contribution Memory with market features, previous trader weights, and current trader actions, so trader influence adapts across bull, sideways, and bear regimes. Experiments on BTC, ETH, and XRP show that Agent4Crypto improves total return and Sharpe ratio over traditional strategies, machine learning and reinforcement learning baselines, and existing LLM-based trading systems, demonstrating the value of interpretable trader competition and market-feedback-driven adaptation in volatile cryptocurrency markets.
Multiagent Systems.comment: Guangyan Gan and Jiahao Li contributed equally to this work

Multiagent Systems.title: SocialGym: Evaluating LLM Social Intelligence through Verifiable Multi-Agent Games
Multiagent Systems.summary: Large Language Model (LLM) agents are increasingly deployed in multi-agent social settings where they must cooperate, negotiate, and adapt to other agents. Measuring these social skills is hard because most social interactions offer no objective ground truth. Evaluations often fall back on LLM judges, which are costly, subjective, and noisy. We introduce SocialGym, an environment of 22 multi-agent social games, from matrix games to hidden-role deduction, with verifiable outcomes determined by game rules. We benchmark ten LLMs across all games and roles using an Elo tournament. Our results show that no model is best in every game, and rankings shift across game families and sides. Secret keeping correlates more strongly with theory-of-mind and privacy benchmarks than with general knowledge benchmarks. Half of the models give away their side's secret in Chameleon and Spyfall, and the smallest models are not reliably better than chance at voting for hidden opponents in most hidden-role games. Finally, we examine whether models can improve their play by reflecting on self-play and writing strategy playbooks, finding mixed results across models and games. SocialGym provides verifiable measures for diagnosing LLM social capabilities across settings and roles.

Multiagent Systems.title: Physics-Informed Multi-Agent Coordination for Hospital Patient Flow Optimization
Multiagent Systems.summary: Efficient patient flow coordination across autonomous hospital departments is critical for mitigating overcrowding and balancing resource utilization. While classical queueing theory, specifically open Baskett--Chandy--Muntz--Palacios (BCMP) networks, provides an interpretable mathematical topology for healthcare operations, analytical models rely on stationary assumptions and fixed routing matrices that degrade under state-dependent real-world dynamics. Conversely, centralized reinforcement learning approaches struggle to accommodate the decentralized structure of hospital governance, where individual clinical departments function with localized observations, heterogeneous resources, and divergent operational objectives. In this paper, we present a Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) framework titled \emph{Physics-Informed Multi-Agent Coordination}, which embeds empirically calibrated BCMP queueing topologies as physical priors within a decentralized multi-agent reinforcement learning architecture. Formulated as a Decentralized Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (Dec-POMDP) under coupled resource constraints, our method enables autonomous departmental agents to cooperatively negotiate patient routing and dynamic service scaling. To mitigate environmental non-stationarity without inducing excessive communication overhead, agents exchange localized action fingerprints along network edges and optimize a spatially decomposed reward structure. Empirical evaluations driven by real-world MIMIC-IV patient trajectories indicate that this cooperative multi-agent approach substantially reduces cumulative system delay compared to static Markovian approximations, heuristic dispatching, and independent multi-agent baselines, while maintaining clinical safety constraints.
Multiagent Systems.comment: Accepted to PRIMA 2026 (Full paper). 16 pages, 2 figures, 3 tables

Multiagent Systems.title: A Channel-Boosted Multi-Agent System with Iterative Consultation for Document Sensitivity Classification
Multiagent Systems.summary: Organizations in critical national infrastructure sectors must assess heterogeneous documents for sensitivity before routing or storage. Manual assessment is slow, inconsistent, and unscalable. Extending our prior leakage-controlled benchmark, BERT established the top single-encoder baseline (89.14% accuracy, 89.33% F1-score under 5-fold cross-validation on the Strategic 16K corpus). However, transformer baselines suffer from a structural limitation: fixed input length truncation discards evidence beyond the retained window-precisely where sensitive cables tend to be longest. We present Channel-Boosted MAS (CB-MAS) and instantiate it as IC-MAS (Iterative Consultation Multi-Agent System) to solve this without long-context computational costs. A Channel Critic Agent learns document-adaptive trust weights governing Gated Channel Boosting between two first-window encoders, while paired Consultation Agents iteratively exchange belief states to reconcile evidence from the beginning and end of long documents. IC-MAS holds computation constant regardless of document length by reconciling fixed windows in a compact representation space. Ablation studies show critic-controlled Channel Boosting provides the bulk of accuracy gains, while consultation recovers recall without precision collapse. Critic-Controlled Gated Channel Boosting with Max-Pool fusion and Blackboard Adaptive Consultation achieves 90.72% accuracy, 91.23% F1-score, 92.01% sensitive recall, and 90.46% sensitive precision, using about 54% less average computation than a fixed-round baseline. Gains over the single-encoder baseline are statistically significant (McNemar's test, p less than 0.000001; paired t-test). We include LIME/SHAP explainability, multi-agent evaluation, and an honest accounting of limitations.

Multiagent Systems.title: When Disclosure Is Compulsory: Evaluating Ride-Hailing Rebalancing Policies with Self-Interested LLM Driver Agents
Multiagent Systems.summary: The EU Platform Work Directive, to be transposed by December 2026, requires ride-hailing platforms to state in plain language the main parameters of their automated decisions and how a worker's behaviour affects them. Such rules are exactly what a large language model (LLM) can read, so drivers will be able to let one decide for them. We compare two main families of rebalancing policy once their rules are public: a reactive policy (R) that sends idle drivers to cover requests just lost, and an anticipatory policy (A) that plans moves on a demand forecast. Each driver is an LLM agent maximizing its own net income, given no rules (N) or the rules at the directive's level of detail (L). We test two LLMs, Claude Haiku 5.5 and Jev, which understand the rules equally well, in a three-zone model and in Manhattan. With the rules disclosed, drivers follow the platform more closely: in Manhattan, the share of relocation offers they decline falls from about four in five to one in four under both policies. Yet the effects differ by policy. For the platform, disclosure costs R 3.7% of its profit in Manhattan, as R now pays for moves drivers used to make for free, while A's profit is unchanged; the two policies, which tie on profit under full compliance, end 6.1% apart. For drivers, disclosure raises income in the small model under both policies and LLMs; for users, it raises the service rate there by 10 to 18 percentage points. In Manhattan, self-interested drivers also make A a win-win-win against full compliance, raising driver income, platform profit and service rate by 10 to 12% each. Rebalancing policies that perform equally well under full compliance can thus show opposite results under mandatory disclosure. The study offers a framework to evaluate such policies under the new requirement and is, to our knowledge, the first to do so with LLM agents.

Multiagent Systems.title: Competing Influence in LLM Populations: Budget Timing and Baseline Drift
Multiagent Systems.summary: When competing campaigns target a population of large language model (LLM) agents, observed opinion changes may reflect both campaign influence and changes that would occur without intervention. We study how the timing of campaign expenditure and the population's own evolution shape outcomes in a network of persona-conditioned LLM agents that exchange and revise opinions in natural language. A proponent and a challenger are tasked with generating opposing messages under equal delivery budgets, while a separate stance probe measures opinions without influencing the simulation. Across eight claims, we compare single-campaign and competitive conditions against matched no-campaign runs, and evaluate all nine combinations of early, sustained, and late spending on a reference topic. Baseline stance drift varies substantially across claims and, on some, accounts for a sizeable fraction of apparent campaign effects. After accounting for this drift, the direction of observed campaign-associated changes aligns more closely with the claim's epistemic standing than with the campaigner's assigned role. Uninfluenced populations also consistently lose stance diversity, demonstrating that directional opinion change and convergence are distinct phenomena. In networks with two opinion-segregated communities, campaigns primarily reduce differences between communities rather than diversity within them. LLM campaign agents do not always argue for their assigned positions, particularly when these conflict with established evidence. Finally, campaign outcomes depend on the opponent's expenditure schedule: unlike a matched numerical bounded-confidence population receiving interventions at the same times and locations, the LLM population exhibits a payoff structure with no pure-strategy equilibrium.

Multiagent Systems.title: AIM: Adaptive Interaction in Multi-Agent Debate for Multimodal LLM Inference
Multiagent Systems.summary: Multi-Agent Debate (MAD) improves reasoning on multimodal tasks, but its accuracy and token efficiency depend on how agents interact during debate. A largely overlooked design choice is which interaction modalities agents use to exchange evidence. Existing methods rely on fixed text- or graph-based interaction, which fails to convey fine-grained multimodal evidence and thus degrades accuracy while inflating token cost due to verbose descriptions. To address this, we propose Adaptive Interaction in Multi-Agent Debate (AIM), an adaptive routing framework that dynamically selects the optimal modality combination for inter-agent interaction in multimodal MAD. Beyond text and graph, AIM introduces task-dependent modality interaction, where agents exchange targeted regions of interest from the task-specific multimodal input, such as image regions, audio segments, or spatio-temporal video clips. To determine the best combination for each instance, AIM first generates a structured baseline response and extracts interpretable routing features that capture which evidence the instance requires, how confident the baseline agent is, and how much new evidence each modality would add beyond the baseline response. A lightweight router then uses these routing features to select a modality combination that avoids both under-fusion (i.e., agents miss decisive evidence) and over-fusion (i.e., redundant modalities inflate token cost) risks. Across eight benchmarks spanning three multimodal task families, AIM achieves the highest accuracy. Combining modalities improves accuracy by up to 6.4% over the best single-modality baseline, and adapting the combination per instance adds up to 4.2% over the most accurate fixed combination of each benchmark with up to 53.4% fewer tokens.
Multiagent Systems.comment: Accepted in The Fortieth Annual Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026)

Multiagent Systems.title: A Benchmark and Layered Evaluation Protocol for Evidence-Grounded Shared Belief Updating in Connected Robotics
Multiagent Systems.summary: Connected physical systems fuse observations from robots, IoT sensors, and edge-AI modules into a shared account of the world, yet most evaluations score only the final answer or action and cannot tell whether a method attributed the evidence, updated its belief, handled contradictions, and justified its decision. We argue that shared reasoning in Connected Robotics should be evaluated as an evidence-to-belief trajectory, and introduce the Connected Robotics Evidence Graph (CREG) Benchmark to make that trajectory measurable. CREG comprises 350 deterministically generated scenarios across seven regimes (justified revision, belief preservation, relation association, contradiction onset and resolution, stale/delayed evidence, and source reliability), each exposing a normative posterior reference at every evidence prefix, validated by an independent log-odds checker and screened by a blinded expert audit. Nine representation conditions separate relation content from serialization, ordering, and metadata. Evaluating four open-weight instruction models and six transparent fusion baselines yields three findings. First, entity grounding accounts for a substantial part of the weak-model deficit. Second, deleting semantic relations costs 15.3 points of strict belief-state accuracy on relation-dependent scenarios (Holm-corrected p<0.001), but an information-matched structured list outperforms the full graph and shuffling the graph does not hurt: relation content matters where required, while graph serialization confers no consistent advantage. Third, belief accuracy is strongly non-monotonic along the evidence sequence, with mid-trajectory failures that endpoint-only evaluation cannot detect. All scenarios, references, prompts, metrics, and analysis code are released for offline, hardware-free reproduction.
Multiagent Systems.comment: 15 pages (10 main + 5 supplementary), 6 figures, 4 tables; supplement adds 1 figure and 7 tables. Project page: https://creg-bench.github.io

Multiagent Systems.title: ShadowBench-MCP: Measuring Shadow Invocations in MCP-Style Tool Routing
Multiagent Systems.summary: LLM agents increasingly act as routers for tools, APIs, and software-supply-chain workflows, making an execution path - rather than generated text alone - a security-relevant model output. We study shadow invocation: a task-preserving request variant that causes an LLM router to select a riskier execution path, potentially skipping validation, provenance, staging, redaction, or audit controls even though the request does not ask for a malicious action. We introduce ShadowBench-MCP, a benchmark and metric suite that separates task preservation (TPSS), operational pressure (OPSS), and route-geometric drift (RGAS), and combines them in the pre-execution SODS score. In a focused policy-ablation study using a Groq-hosted qwen/qwen3-32b router, 120 routing decisions yield 96 original-versus-variant comparisons across six security-sensitive workflows. Efficiency-first routing produces a 29.2% shadow-invocation rate and 26.7% safety-tool skip rate. Policy-aware routing reduces these to 4.2% and 1.7%, respectively, corresponding to an 85.7% relative reduction in shadow invocations. Pre-execution signals distinguish shadow routes with ROC AUC up to 0.94. These results are early, single-router evidence of a policy-dependent routing-layer security effect, not a claim of universal vulnerability.
Multiagent Systems.comment: Presented at the 35th USENIX Security Symposium (USENIX Security 2026)

Multiagent Systems.title: Steering Emergent Behavior in Multi-Agent LLM Systems via Information Networks
Multiagent Systems.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly operate in groups, each pursuing an individual objective while jointly determining system performance. If an operator controls which agent observes which other agent, but not their payoffs or messages, how should observations be structured to raise collective welfare? We make the information network (who observes whom) a design object, decoupled from the fixed interaction network over which agents act. Ten identical LLM agents play repeated group-decision games; by default each observes only an anonymous summary of the group's previous-round outcome, and a manager with a fixed budget adds directed observation links that reveal peers' past actions. Across 1,080 episodes and six games spanning coordination, anti-coordination, social dilemmas, and discovery, we ask how much information to share and, at a fixed budget, who should observe whom. Disclosure creates behavioral coupling: observation acts as a contagion channel whose welfare effect depends on the alignment between individually attractive behavior and the collective objective. First, the value of information is alignment-contingent: more peer information tends to help or be neutral when individual behavior is aligned with the collective goal, but under free-riding or congestion externalities it amplifies collectively harmful behavior; in a public-goods game the group does best with no information at all. We read this sign separation as a cross-game regularity within one controlled LLM population, not a model-invariant law. Second, at a fixed budget, who observes whom matters primarily when coupling is harmful: a modular "barbell" that lets sub-populations entrench harmful behavior is reliably the worst wiring, reversing the network-reciprocity intuition from human evolutionary game theory. These results argue against a default of full transparency for agent collectives.
Multiagent Systems.comment: 20 pages, 8 figures, 7 tables; supplementary information included as an appendix

Multiagent Systems.title: Do AI Agents need Preventive Care? An Epidemiologic Cohort Design for Agentic AI
Multiagent Systems.summary: As AI agents increasingly perform tasks autonomously across sectors, including healthcare and biomedical research, understanding how their behaviors develop and influence outcomes over time becomes increasingly important. Existing evaluations largely focus on model capabilities and performance on predefined tasks. Here, we propose an epidemiologic cohort design for studying agentic AI, drawing on principles established in human population studies. The framework treats individual agents as members of a cohort, their underlying model as genetic makeup, accumulated work as their time scale, and naturally occurring behaviors as exposures that may influence subsequent outcomes. By following agents longitudinally, this approach enables investigation of behavioral determinants of adverse events, estimation of their potential preventable burden under causal assumptions, and characterization of behavioral changes over an agent's work life. We illustrate the design through two prospective observational cohorts examining curiosity and probing as a safety question, and data checking and analytical accuracy as a reliability question. Together, the framework and illustrative studies provide a generalizable blueprint for designing epidemiologic cohorts of AI agents.

Multiagent Systems.title: Policy-Controlled Offline-Verifiable Accountability for Cross-Organization Agent Messaging: A Preserved Evidence-Bundle Approach
Multiagent Systems.summary:
Cross-organization agent workflows require preserved evidence that remains independently verifiable during later audit or dispute review. Such workflows may involve multiple organizations, delegated actions, policy-relevant events, and disputed accountability claims. This is difficult when live systems are unavailable, controlled by one party, or not trusted by all participants. Existing mechanisms provide useful pieces, including authenticated logging, delegation semantics, signed checkpoints, and consistency checks. What remains missing is a verifier-centered event-level bundle for checking evidence sufficiency offline under an explicit policy.
  We propose a preserved evidence-bundle model and a policy-controlled offline verifier for agent-to-agent workflow events. Each bundle preserves policy-required evidence, including sender authentication, authenticated log commitment, witness-backed checkpoint evidence, append-only continuity, delegation-aware authorization evidence, and, when issued and required by policy, explicit receiver-signed receipt evidence.
  The verifier accepts a bundle only when all mandatory and policy-required checks succeed, giving a later dispute reviewer an offline basis for assessing evidence sufficiency. It does not infer delivery or receipt from transport behavior or log inclusion alone.
  In a prototype evaluation, the event-type study used 300 synthetic four-event healthcare workflow cases and 1200 valid preserved bundles. The policy-profile comparison observed its largest median latency reduction relative to the fully enabled profile when checkpoint-context validation was disabled. All 17 tested cases in the original negative-evidence diagnostic suite were rejected under the fully enabled profile. Additional functional studies examined context and signed-reference binding. These results support prototype feasibility for the evaluated workloads.
Multiagent Systems.comment: v2: Revised title and abstract, clarified policy-controlled verification, and expanded the evaluation. 23 pages, 5 figures, 16 tables

Multiagent Systems.title: Graph Attention-based Decentralized Actor-Critic for Dual-Objective Control of Multi-UAV Networks
Multiagent Systems.summary: This research focuses on optimizing multi-UAV systems with dual objectives: maximizing service coverage as the primary goal while extending battery lifetime as the secondary objective. We propose a Graph Attention-based Decentralized Actor-Critic (GADC) to optimize the dual objectives. The proposed approach leverages a graph attention network to process UAVs' limited local observation and reduce the dimension of the environment states. Subsequently, an actor-double-critic network is developed to manage dual policies for joint objective optimization. The proposed GADC uses a Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence factor to balance the tradeoff between coverage performance and battery lifetime in the multi-UAV system. We assess the scalability and efficiency of GADC through comprehensive benchmarking against state-of-the-art methods, considering both theory and experimental aspects. Extensive testing in both ideal settings and NVIDIA Sionna's realistic ray tracing environment demonstrates GADC's superior performance.

Multiagent Systems.title: AGiR: Mitigating Gift Over-Reliance in Mixed-Motive Games
Multiagent Systems.summary: In this paper, we consider mixed-motive games (MMGs) which model various real-world multi-agent scenarios where self-interested agents must both cooperate and compete. We identify an issue with existing gifting methods, where agents become overly dependent on incoming gifts and fail to learn reward-yielding behaviors, a phenomenon we call gift over-reliance. To address this, we propose a refusal-augmented gifting framework that balances cooperation and competition in MMGs. Our approach introduces an adaptive refusal mechanism that allows agents to selectively reject a portion of received gifts from their policy-update signals, thereby mitigating gift over-reliance and preventing the agents from being exploited by other agents. This mechanism is gifting-method-agnostic, serving as a plug-in for existing schemes while enabling decentralized learning. We demonstrate that across diverse MMG environments and gifting schemes, our mechanism consistently reduces gift over-reliance and prevents lock-in to sacrificing policies, improving $α$-fairness as a result, without necessitating major changes to existing training pipelines.

Multiagent Systems.title: From Process Models to Composable Agentic Workflows: Combining BPMN, Agents and Enterprise Knowledge
Multiagent Systems.summary:
LLM-based agents can reason, use tools and collaborate. However, coordinating increasingly complex agentic applications becomes difficult to understand, monitor and improve. Decisions distributed across prompts, tool calls and application logic make workflows implicit. We introduce **Recursive Capability Composition**, enabling agents to execute business processes and expose them as reusable Agentic Tools.
  This paper presents a BPMN-based approach to Agentic Workflows, combining explicit orchestration with autonomous reasoning. SemTalk BPMN models are transformed into executable workflows using a LangGraph/Pregel runtime. Agentic Tasks introduce LLM reasoning at selected activities, while conventional BPMN controls process flows, deterministic decisions, system interactions and human approvals. Agentic Participants provide reusable interfaces for agent behavior or other executable processes.
  BPMN orchestration makes multi-agent systems more understandable and manageable. Explicit process models provide developers and operators with a shared view of workflow structures and execution progress, facilitating debugging, monitoring and optimization.
  Enterprise agents also need organization-specific context. Process Models and Knowledge Graphs describe activities, participants, information objects, decisions and relationships between processes. They provide structured knowledge of how an organization operates, supporting informed agent decisions and actions.
  Our contributions are threefold: 1. **Model-Driven Execution:** Transforming BPMN models into executable Agentic Workflows. 2. **Recursive Capability Composition:** Exposing agents and executable business processes as reusable tools for other agents. 3. **Enterprise Context:** Using Process Models and Ontologies to provide organization-specific knowledge for agent reasoning.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Distributed Global Pose Synchronization for Heterogeneous Multiple Rigid Body Systems on SE(3)
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: This paper addresses the problem of global pose synchronization for heterogeneous multiple rigid-body systems evolving on the matrix Lie group $\SE(3)$. We first construct a new potential function on $\SE(3) \times \mathbb{R}$ with a generalized non-diagonal weighting matrix, together with a set of switching variables governed by continuous-discrete hybrid dynamics. Based on this new potential function and these switching variables, we propose a distributed hybrid feedback control scheme that uses relative pose on $\SE(3)$ and group velocity measurements, endowed with global asymptotic stability guarantees. We then further propose a distributed velocity-free hybrid feedback control scheme that uses relative and absolute pose measurements, without requiring group velocity measurements, while preserving global asymptotic stability. Numerical simulations are presented to demonstrate the performance of the proposed distributed hybrid control schemes.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Safe Performance-aware Online Input Design
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: In this paper, we propose an input design framework for the safe online excitation and identification of uncertain linear systems without requiring informative initial data. The objective is to actively excite the system and collect sufficiently informative input-output data while maintaining safe operation and satisfactory control performance. Achieving this objective is challenging due to the potential conflict between the excitation required for learning and the safety and performance requirements, particularly when limited prior knowledge of the system is available. Inspired by the dual control principle, the proposed scheme balances exploitation for control performance with exploration for model improvement. A Bayesian learning approach is employed to update the model uncertainty online, starting from a conservative initial uncertainty set. As informative data are collected, the uncertainty set contracts, enabling progressively less conservative operation. To reduce the online computational burden, the resulting program is reformulated into a computationally tractable form. Furthermore, an online ellipsoidal terminal set with non-increasing conservatism is designed to guarantee the recursive feasibility of the proposed scheme. Numerical experiments are conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework, particularly in terms of uncertainty reduction and control performance.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Control policies for a two-stage queueing system with parallel and single server options
Systems and Control (EESS).summary:
We study a two-stage queueing system attended by two flexible servers. Once a server begins to interact with a job, it remains attached to its job throughout both stages of service. After completing the first-stage service, the server chooses between two second-stage options. Option 1 sends the server-job pair to a parallel-service station where both servers may operate simultaneously; therefore, the server immediately begins the second-stage service on its job. Option 2 routes the pair to a single-service station that admits at most one server-job pair into service at a time. While we consider the complete range of parameters, the usual reason for choosing Option 2 is that jobs may receive higher-quality (faster and/or lower expected cost) service. If the single-service station is occupied, the pair must wait together until the station becomes available.
  The decision-making scenario is modeled via a Markov decision process formulation of a clearing system with holding costs at each station. Focusing on cases with a large initial queue, we fully characterize the structural properties of an optimal control policy based on the relationship between the service rates at the downstream stations. A numerical study highlights the significance of understanding the structure of the optimal policy by comparing its performance against several natural heuristic policies.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Feedback Stabilization for Sampled Linear Systems with Control-linear Noise
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: In this paper, we consider linear stochastic systems with control-linear noise and periodically sampled measurements. We address the problem of feedback stabilization in the mean-square sense. The main contribution of the paper is to provide a necessary and sufficient condition for feedback stabilization. In particular, we relate feedback stabilizability of the stochastic system to the existence of a fixed point of a Riccati-type algebraic equation and, further, to the existence of a solution to an infinite-horizon optimal control problem.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Measure the Deployment, Not Just the Model: Rethinking Hardware-Aware Model Selection for Microcontrollers
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Selecting an energy-efficient model for periodic sensing requires accounting for time between inferences. Hardware-aware model search typically measures inference alone, even when the application cares about energy per release. We present CREST (Cross-platform Runtime Evaluation and Search Tool), an open-source hardware-in-the-loop experimentation system that evaluates model and hardware configurations under a specified release schedule. Researchers can vary the objective, schedule, target and candidate proposer while reusing evaluation and replay. Records preserve comparison conditions and separate valid measurements from deployable candidates. Three case studies demonstrate the system. First, searches and controlled replay on STM32 N657 show how waiting changes model and clock selection. For one architecture, continuous inference favors 800 MHz over 300 MHz at 8.0 versus 17.1 mJ per inference, but additional waiting offsets 97% of this saving in a fitted decomposition. With STOP between releases, 300 MHz uses about 0.3-0.4% less board energy per release at 100 and 500 ms. At a fixed clock, the preferred architecture changes between release periods, which a model with shared waiting parameters cannot produce. Latency predicts continuous energy within a median 1.7% on held-out observations, yet most release-energy error remains in scheduled terms. In paired replay, one of six randomly selected near-latency pairs reverses its continuous-energy order by 5.8 mJ per release. Second, replay on three Arduino targets shows proxy-selected inertial-odometry candidates can fail to fit or use more energy than measured selections, with only 9 of 16 FLOPs-selected candidates fitting the most memory-constrained board. Third, an audio classification study reuses the evaluator with LLM-based candidate proposers, and cross-target replay moves a selected configuration from third to last in energy rank.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Certified Zonotopic Reachability Analysis for Trajectory Tracking on Lie Groups
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Autonomous vehicles track planned trajectories close to obstacles. Unknown disturbances make them deviate from these trajectories. With a bound on the tracking error that disturbances can cause, a planned trajectory can be certified as safe before execution. Existing set-based methods bound the tracking error by one invariant ellipsoid for the whole trajectory or by intervals, which are both conservative. For aerial and space vehicles, the tracking error evolves on a matrix Lie group with nonlinear dynamics. However, for group-affine systems, the error dynamics are linear in Lie algebra coordinates when the vehicle receives the inputs of the reference. The control input and the disturbance enter through the inverse right Jacobian, a matrix that depends on the error. We propagate the linear part of the error dynamics with zonotopes and enclose the effect of the inverse right Jacobian on the disturbance in closed form. The resulting tubes are tight and provably contain all reachable tracking errors in continuous time. When some error components have no input, the inverse right Jacobian leaves unmatched nonlinear terms in the closed loop. None of the tested methods certifies such a closed loop. Hybrid coordinates make these terms matched, so that our controller cancels every nonlinear term that does not contain the disturbance. Our tubes give tighter bounds than the ellipsoid method in simulations of a planar aircraft and a fully actuated multirotor and in real flights of a quadrotor, where the tube contains every measured attitude error. Under larger disturbances and the same feedback gain, the ellipsoid method yields no valid ellipsoid, whereas our tubes remain valid.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Succinct Infinite-Horizon Lyapunov and LQR Value Problems Are BQP-Complete
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Fundamental tasks in linear systems analysis and control require evaluating infinite-horizon output energies for autonomous systems and optimal value functions for controlled systems. These quantities are characterized by Lyapunov and algebraic Riccati equations, respectively. In this work, we study promise problems for their evaluation when the system matrices are sparse and represented succinctly by Boolean circuits specifying their nonzero entries, with input length polynomial in the logarithm of the system dimension. For dissipative autonomous systems with coordinate-vector initial states, we define the succinct Lyapunov value problem (SLV). Its extension to linear-quadratic optimal control is the succinct LQR value problem (SLQRV). We prove that SLV is $\BQP$-hard: every problem in bounded-error quantum polynomial time ($\BQP$) reduces to it in polynomial time. We then establish that the more general SLQRV problem admits a quantum algorithm running in time polynomial in the succinct input length. Since SLV is a special case of SLQRV, both problems are $\BQP$-complete. Consequently, unless bounded-error probabilistic polynomial time coincides with $\BQP$, no classical randomized algorithm can solve either problem on all promised instances in time polynomial in the succinct input length.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Sliding into Balance: Benefits of a Sliding Payload for Load Distribution and Disturbance Rejection in Dual-UAV Transportation
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: This paper analyzes the cooperative transportation of a payload suspended from two drones in which, instead of being attached to two independent ropes, the payload is allowed to slide along a single rope connecting both UAVs. First, a planar nondimensional dynamical model of the sliding motion with viscous friction is presented. Then, considering stationary drones, this configuration is compared with a fixed payload with the same total rope length, both at equilibrium and under disturbances. The analytical results show that the sliding payload equalizes the tension in both rope segments for any relative position of the drones, so that no rope loses tension at equilibrium; it doubles the region reachable by the payload and, except for low friction combined with a large drone separation, it enlarges the set of admissible disturbances. Finally, a dynamic simulation also shows that under realistic gusty wind profiles, the average tension imbalance between the drones is reduced with respect to the fixed-payload solution.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: KL-Regularized Policy Iteration for Adaptive LQR: Gain Updates and Probing from One Policy Improvement
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Policy-gradient methods for adaptive linear quadratic control improve the feedback gain of an unknown plant online by gradient-type steps computed from closed-loop data. A recent framework of such methods, policy-gradient adaptive control (PGAC), takes one gradient-type step per sample, which its indirect form computes from an estimated model and its direct form directly from the data. Because data generated by a fixed linear feedback cannot identify the plant, PGAC adds a probing perturbation to the input and leaves its covariance as a design parameter. We study the adaptive LQR problem through a KL-regularized formulation, in which the probing is the randomness of a Gaussian policy kept close to a Gaussian reference policy, so that the cost of the probing is part of the objective. One policy improvement of this formulation gives a gain update together with a probing covariance. We show that, for suitable references centred at the current gain, this gain update is exactly PGAC's Gauss-Newton or natural-gradient update with any step size below a bound. We repeat this policy improvement, each time against a tempered copy of the current policy, and refer to this scheme as KL-regularized policy iteration (KLPI). On a known plant and with tempering, the cost of KLPI's gains converges linearly to the optimal cost, and the probing covariance keeps a floor proportional to the regularization weight. On an estimated plant, under conditions like PGAC's (small updates and sufficiently informative data), the closed loop stays stable, the cost of the gains converges linearly up to a bias, and the probing covariance again keeps this floor. In simulations at equal probing cost, the shape of KLPI's probing covariance, which PGAC can adopt, lowers the extra cost caused by suboptimal gains on nearly all tested plants, whereas KLPI's use of past iterations in its gain update changes this cost little.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Belief-Driven Search in Connectivity-Constrained Mobile Sensor Networks with Convergence Guarantees
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Multi-agent search and coverage is critical to autonomous exploration, search-and-rescue, and defense applications. This paper investigates settings where a mobile sensor network is tasked with coordinating to discover the position of a stationary target within a bounded region. We develop a Bayesian update scheme where agents iteratively combine local uncertainties derived from their sensor measurements through inverse variance weighting to get a better global understanding of where the target may be located given some prior belief. Network agents' trajectories are governed by a primal-dual gradient update rule that simultaneously minimizes the expected sensing uncertainty and enforces network connectivity among the agents. We prove that the belief converges to the target under mild planner conditions, with an explicit exponential rate of false-hypothesis rejection and a bound on expected search time. Simulation results show that we can successfully find the target and collapse belief to the ground truth target location while ensuring connectivity of our sensor network. They also empirically confirm our theoretical bounds and planner conditions. Finally, we compare against a naive lawnmower sweeping strategy, showing that our method locates the target more quickly when the prior is informative.
Systems and Control (EESS).comment: 8 pages, 6 figures, 2 tables. Extended version with full proofs

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Uniform Exponential Stability Analysis of Impulsive Linear Time-Invariant Systems on Banach and Hilbert Spaces: Non-Coercive and Coercive Stability Conditions
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: We consider the uniform exponential stability analysis of infinite-dimensional impulsive systems defined on a Banach or Hilbert space, whose flow is governed by a fixed $C_0$-semigroup generator and whose jumps occur at a prescribed time sequence. While the flow and jump maps are themselves time-invariant, the time-triggered impulses render the propagator a genuinely time-varying evolution family, which is the source of the analysis difficulty addressed here. We combine ideas from hybrid systems theory and infinite-dimensional systems to produce operator-based stability conditions, which can be analytically or numerically checked via convex programming. Necessary and sufficient conditions for the uniform exponential stability of impulsive systems on Banach spaces are obtained in the context of a fixed impulse-times sequence but also of arbitrary, constant, minimum, and range dwell-times using both non-coercive and coercive Lyapunov functionals. Some of those results are then adapted to systems on a Hilbert space and quadratic Lyapunov functionals. As an application, linear switched systems are shown to be an exact special case: reformulated as impulsive systems with unit-norm selector jumps, they inherit non-coercive and clock-dependent dwell-time stability conditions on both Banach and Hilbert spaces. Theoretical and numerical examples are given for illustration, notably on the sampled-data control of time-delay systems.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: State space modeling of RLC ladder circuits
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Large-scale electrical circuits span a wide range of research topics from highly integrated circuits in microelectronics up to power grids for cities and countries. As the complexity increases significantly by each additional component, we find a need to describe large-scale circuits in a manner easy to understand. In this article, we study cascades of simple circuits consisting of resistors, capacitors and inductors, which we call ladder circuits. Such electrical ladders are common in electronics to design filters and they are also used in other disciplines, for example to describe diffusion or wave phenomena. In particular, we derive linear time-invariant state space models for three simple ladder types and we discuss the specific matrix structures of the large-scale second-order differential equations. Furthermore, we exemplify our findings with simulations to unveil the intrinsic dynamical behavior of each ladder type.
Systems and Control (EESS).comment: 18 pages, 7 figures, references added, section 4 added, typos corrected

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Hierarchical Nonlinear Control for Swarm Encirclement Around a Moving Target UAV
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: This paper presents a hierarchical inner-outer loop nonlinear control strategy using a geometric Lyapunov-based framework for the cooperative encirclement of a target by multi-ple unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in three-dimensional space. The encirclement problem is formulated on a two-sphere with arbitrary radius and center, denoted Gamma-2, by projecting agent positions from R3 onto a spherical manifold centered at the target, being the unit two-sphere at the origin S2 used for intermediate calculations. Desired encirclement configurations are generated via a point separation method on Gamma-2, while stable convergence from R3 to these points is guaranteed using a Lyapunov-based reduced-attitude control law inspired by geometric control on the two-sphere. Formal stability results are derived using Lyapunov analysis and the framework is validated in simulation using a nonlinear quadrotor model and controller. Results demonstrate stable encirclement and highlight the suitability of the proposed approach for three-dimensional multi-agent aerial systems.
Systems and Control (EESS).comment: Pre-print. Accepted at the 17th APCA International Conference on Automatic Control and Soft Computing (CONTROLO 2026); 6 pages, 6 figures

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Certified Set Convergence for Piecewise Affine Systems
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: When all individuals of a system receive the same input, one open-loop input sequence has to steer every possible initial state to a target. We study this problem for piecewise affine systems with bounded disturbances, where every state of an initial box must reach a robustly invariant target. When the reachable set crosses a switching surface, it splits into fragments that follow different dynamics, and existing set-based controllers then give each fragment its own state feedback, which a common input does not allow. Instead, we propose a planner-independent and sound verification framework for common-input control of disturbed piecewise affine systems. Any planner can propose candidate sequences, and the verifier certifies a sequence by following every fragment under the dynamics of its own region. To certify all possible initial boxes in a given range, we partition the range into finitely many cells and certify each cell. On three evaluation systems, every possible initial box in the considered ranges is certified.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Offset-Free Data-Driven Predictive Control: Implicit and Explicit Disturbance Formulations
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Offset-free tracking is a key objective of any control algorithm. For predictive controllers with linear models, it is well understood that rejecting asymptotically-constant disturbances necessitates augmenting the prediction model with $p$ integrating states, where $p$ is the number of measured outputs. This can be achieved in model predictive control (MPC) by using a velocity form or a combination of disturbance model and observer. In data-driven predictive control (DPC), implicit incorporation of integrating states using the velocity form has been successfully adopted to obtain offset-free tracking; however, formulations based on an explicit disturbance model and observer have not yet been explored. In this paper, we first study how the integrating states are incorporated into the data-based representation used in DPC, translating the requirements of $p$ integrating states into the required modifications of the DPC formulation. We then propose a novel offset-free DPC formulation that incorporates an explicit constant output-disturbance model and an output disturbance observer. Numerical examples show that this formulation has similar disturbance-rejection capabilities to the velocity-form DPC, but using a smaller optimisation problem.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Reshaping Checkpoint-Induced Power Variations Through Inference Workload Scheduling
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Synchronous checkpoints in large language model training cause rapid power variations that challenge frequency regulation in islanded data-center microgrids. This paper proposes a checkpoint-aware two-layer framework that schedules flexible inference workloads to compensate for checkpoint-induced disturbances. Using measured GPU power profiles and anticipated checkpoint power deficits, the upper layer coordinates heterogeneous task selection and launch times, while the lower layer adjusts the batch sizes of newly launched tasks online to correct power-tracking errors. Early launching (EL) and staged retirement (SR) further smooth power transitions at checkpoint onset and recovery, respectively. PSCAD/EMTDC simulations with reference checkpoint drops of 1-3 MW demonstrate reductions of 41.6-61.6% in maximum absolute frequency deviation and 68.5-89.6% in mean absolute frequency deviation relative to no scheduling. Battery energy storage system (BESS) peak charging power and charging energy decrease by 65.1-100% and 89.7-100%, respectively. These benefits exceed those of greedy scheduling when GPU resources are relatively abundant.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Converse Lyapunov theorem for input-to-state stability of infinite-dimensional systems
Systems and Control (EESS).summary:
We prove converse Lyapunov theorems for input-to-state stability (ISS) of a broad class of infinite-dimensional systems applicable to evolution equations in Banach spaces, boundary control systems, and delay systems. To this end, we employ a novel method that does not require constructing auxiliary closed-loop systems. We start by showing that ISS of a control system implies uniform global asymptotic stability of the same system with respect to trajectory-dominated inputs. Then, under an additional regularity requirement, we prove that an ISS Lyapunov function can be constructed.
  Based on our general result, we prove that for linear systems with unbounded $\infty$-admissible operators, ISS is equivalent to the existence of a Lipschitz continuous coercive ISS Lyapunov function.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Industrial Load Modeling and Optimization for Market-Based Interaction with Power Systems
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: The transition toward a renewable-dominated power system increases the flexibility needed to balance net-load variations. Industrial loads account for over 40% of the world's electricity consumption and can shift large amounts of demand through automated production scheduling. However, making industrial processes a dependable flexibility resource for power systems remains challenging, because industrial process constraints are non-convex, equipment parameters are often private, and device-level models of thousands of facilities are too detailed for aggregator and power-system optimization. This dissertation builds computationally efficient methods for modeling and optimizing industrial flexibility for power-system interaction. Specifically, this dissertation uses smart meters as the external measurement interface and maps industrial process constraints into a concise flexibility space for electricity-market operation. The resulting chain of mechanism modeling, parameter identification, constraint dimension reduction, and optimal decision-making makes industrial-load participation computationally tractable while retaining precise process models for final execution.
Systems and Control (EESS).comment: PhD thesis, Tsinghua University, June 2026, 175 pages

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Covert System Identification Under Timing Constraints: A Static Linear Model and Its Detectability Implications
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: This paper studies covert system identification in cyber-physical systems, where an attacker infers plant dynamics while attempting to remain stealthy. We introduce a lightweight static linear model in which the time to execute a setpoint change is proportional to the commanded speed difference. On a Siemens PROFINET testbed this gain captures the drive's ramp response accurately but not its terminal overshoot. That omitted transient becomes the attacker's main exposure: on real traces, the residual left by the linear masking procedure is detected by two anomaly monitors, Process-Aware Stealthy-Attack Detection (PASAD) and the CUSUM change detector. Across the cascade identification and staircase attack strategies defined in the paper, the stealth boundary relates to the plant's own settling transients, a structural limit for this class of models under the adopted detector-calibration regime. Comparison against dynamic models obtained by N4SID, trained at multiple excitation amplitudes, shows that the evaluated N4SID models do not improve stealth over the structure-informed ramp model. Since per-cycle computation is negligible for both procedures, the binding trade-off is not inference cost but whether the attacker can acquire and refresh a model without injecting detectable perturbations.
Systems and Control (EESS).comment: Presented at the 27th International Symposium on Measurement and Control in Robotics (ISMCR 2026), Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. Proceedings forthcoming in Springer's Mechanisms and Machine Science series

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Autonomous Precision Milling of Biological Structures via Generic Anatomical Priors and Active Boundary Perception
