Systems and Control (EESS).title: Learning the NMPC with Stability Guarantees
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Although nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) is widely used, its online optimization is computationally expensive. Neural network approximations of NMPC can effectively reduce the online computational burden but generally lack stability guarantees. This paper proposes an approximate NMPC framework with guarantees of constraint satisfaction and closed-loop stability. The approximation error is addressed through constraint tightening, and the resulting tightened NMPC is used to generate the training dataset of the approximate NMPC. The maximum allowable approximation error is prescribed a priori for the design of tightened NMPC and satisfied in a probabilistic sense through an iterative trial-and-error procedure alternating between network training and a posteriori verification. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed framework is demonstrated through a numerical example of a constrained nonlinear system.
Systems and Control (EESS).comment: 13 pages, 7 figures, this paper was not presented at any IFAC conference

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Analysis increments for model bias diagnosis and correction: Theoretical foundations
Systems and Control (EESS).summary:
A common method for diagnosing and correcting model bias in weather and climate prediction is based on analysis increments: the difference between the analysis and the forecast at each data assimilation cycle. Their time average is used to estimate and correct the bias, and machine learning is increasingly used to map the forecast state to the increments, giving a state-dependent correction. Despite its widespread use, the method lacks theoretical foundations.
  We first analyse a Kalman filter whose forecast model has a constant bias. We show what the averaged increment measures, and prove that iterating the correction removes all of the bias seen through the observations; for linear dynamics, no method can identify the rest.
  We then extend the analysis to state-dependent biases. For linear dynamics, each increment records the model error over the filter's memory, as seen through the observations. We use this to determine what the increments measure when averaged over a long period, averaged over periods with similar slowly varying conditions, and used without averaging, as in machine-learned corrections.
  Numerical experiments confirm the theory for a linear model and suggest that its main conclusions carry over to the nonlinear Lorenz '96 model, including for a correction learned by a neural network.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Scalable Neural Safety Certification via Monotonicity
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Learning-based safety certification offers a promising route for verifying complex dynamical systems when explicit models are unavailable, but existing data-driven methods often scale poorly: they treat the system as a black box, rely on dense discretizations or Lipschitz bounds, and consequently suffer from sample complexity that grows exponentially with dimension. This paper shows that a common structural property of dynamical systems--monotonicity--can be used to break this curse of dimensionality. We develop a data-driven framework for robust safety verification and safe controller synthesis for unknown monotone systems using only simulator queries. Our main theoretical result proves that, for monotone systems with upper-closed unsafe sets, safety is completely characterized by the existence of monotone inductive barrier certificates. This structure reduces certificate verification over continuous state spaces to localized boundary checks over finitely many cells. To learn such certificates, we introduce Max-Monotone Networks, a monotone neural architecture with universal approximation guarantees for monotone functions. We then propose a training and refinement algorithm that, upon successful termination, returns formally valid neural barrier certificates and, under mild partition assumptions, requires only $O(n)$ simulator queries. Across high-dimensional benchmarks, including oscillator networks with up to $13{,}659$ states and traffic networks with $1{,}000$ states, our method certifies safety in regimes where prior approaches either do not converge or exceed memory limits. These results demonstrate that exploiting order structure can make neural safety certification both scalable and formally sound.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Feasibility-Aware Learning for Network-Constrained Unit Commitment
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Learning-based approaches to network-constrained unit commitment (NCUC) usually still rely on an optimization solver to repair or complete their predictions, which limits the speedup they can deliver. This paper proposes FALCON-UC, a feasibility-aware graph learning framework that predicts commitment and dispatch jointly and produces final schedules without solving a mixed-integer program at inference time. It combines an LSTM--GraphSAGE predictor over a fully connected generator graph, a differentiable correction that embeds commitment-dependent dispatch bounds, power balance, and PTDF-based branch flows in training, and deterministic commitment, dispatch, and ramp-coupled reserve repairs at inference. On the 2383-bus system, FALCON-UC achieves $99.09\%$ commitment accuracy and a $0.4350\%$ mean absolute cost gap with all evaluated constraints within tolerance at $0.0562$ s per instance, a $2.27\times10^{3}$ speedup over the solver. MTLR R-SCUC-FL is slightly more accurate but still needs an optimization solver to complete each schedule, which takes $262.2$ s per instance, $4.67\times10^{3}$ times the FALCON-UC runtime. A label-only baseline without repair violates the balance and branch limits on every 2383-bus test instance, and FALCON-UC also meets all evaluated constraint tolerances on a 1354-bus system.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Distributed Learning of $α$-Potential Functions in Strategic Multi-agent Systems
Systems and Control (EESS).summary:
We study the problem of computing the tightest \(α\)-potential approximation of a general-sum game over continuous action spaces, within a prescribed class of potential functions and when each player has access only to its own utility function. The difficulty is twofold: the approximation error involves a worst-case search over an infinite set of unilateral deviations, and the required utility information is distributed across players.
  For a linear-in-parameters potential class, we use an exact finite-tuple reformulation that separates the problem into a global outer search over deviation tuples and distributed convex inner problems. We develop a primal--dual inner oracle tailored to this structure and establish a uniform one-sided accuracy guarantee. This oracle can be combined with global outer search to obtain an end-to-end guarantee on the outer optimization error. We also develop a projected zeroth-order outer method as a computationally lighter alternative for higher-dimensional problems. Numerical experiments illustrate the accuracy--computation tradeoff between the two outer-search methods and show that the proposed optimization framework can improve upon analytical \(α\)-potential constructions.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Floquet-Parameterized Koopman-MPC for Tracking Periodic Orbits
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Designing real-time control for nonlinear systems to track periodic orbits can be challenging, especially for complex and coupled dynamical systems (e.g., tethered kites), where the true model parameters are hard to obtain. To address this, we propose a physics-informed Koopman learning approach that incorporates periodic-orbit stability directly into the learned linear predictor. The approach combines the underlying periodic structure of the dynamics along with periodic state-input trajectory data to learn physically consistent linear predictors (in lifted/observable space). We leverage Floquet theory, which studies the stability of periodic orbits in nonlinear systems, to obtain the periodic stability information of a given orbit via a monodromy matrix (i.e., the state transition matrix over an entire period). Subsequently, we impose open-loop monodromy constraints to learn Floquet-parameterized linear predictors using a least-squares Extended Dynamic Mode Decomposition (EDMD) formulation, thereby constraining the search space and aiding in Koopman learning. We then utilize these linear predictors to design a model predictive control (MPC) law for tracking periodic references. Finally, we evaluate the designed framework on a cartpole system under periodic forcing and compare it against a purely data-driven baseline.

Multiagent Systems.title: Network Contention State Aware Dynamic Optimizer for Accelerator Collective Communication Libraries
Multiagent Systems.summary: Collective Communication Libraries (CCL) are critical for large-scale distributed AI/ML training, yet their configurations are determined by static heuristics that do not account for real-time network conditions. Our empirical study shows that these heuristics perform near-optimally in contention-free environments, but degrade substantially under background traffic. To address this, we present a cooperative multi-agent run-time optimizer for accelerator collective communication. Our approach employs a two-agent architecture: (i) detector- a Long Short Term Memory(LSTM) recurring neural network fed classifier head with a sequential probability ratio test that distinguishes sustained contention from transient spikes; and (ii) selector- a configuration selector built on a Dueling Double DQN (D3QN) with Conservative Q-Learning that adapts configuration parameters in response. We implemented this dynamic tuner over NCCL, a widely used CCL developed by NVIDIA. When evaluated on Chameleon Cloud's isolated bare-metal cluster, this dynamic tuning approach reduces AllReduce latency by 36% over NCCL and 32% over a fully converged AutoCCL. We further evaluated it across six real AI workloads spanning convolutional networks, transformers, and recommendation architectures. Our multi-agent tuner approach delivers up to 65% speedups on Delta cluster with NVIDIA A100 GPUs and Slingshot-11 fabric internode connectivity.

Multiagent Systems.title: Convergence of Byzantine-Resilient Gradient Tracking via Probabilistic Edge Dropout
Multiagent Systems.summary: We study distributed optimization over networks with Byzantine agents that may send arbitrary adversarial messages. We propose Gradient Tracking with Probabilistic Edge Dropout (GT-PD), which combines a universal self-centred projection that clips incoming messages to a radius-$τ$ ball around the receiver with a fully decentralized probabilistic dropout rule driven by a threshold-gated, dual-metric trust score in the decision and tracking channels. These identity-free defences bound adversarial perturbations while preserving doubly stochastic mixing. The projection preserves the honest network average exactly in every realization, even when honest messages are clipped. Under complete Byzantine isolation ($p_b=0$), GT-PD converges linearly to a neighbourhood of order $ασ^2/(μn_{\mathcal H})$ plus higher-order network terms, matching centralized stochastic gradient descent to first order in the step size. We also give a radius computable from problem data that ensures honest messages remain unclipped with high probability. Under partial isolation ($p_b>0$), a leaky variant, GT-PD-L, controls accumulated tracking perturbations and converges linearly to a bounded neighbourhood governed by stochastic variance and the clipping-to-leak ratio, under explicit conditions on the step size, leak, and aggregate Byzantine mixing weight. With two-tier dropout and $p_h=1$, Byzantine isolation adds no variance to honest consensus dynamics. MNIST experiments under Sign Flip, ALIE, and Inner Product Manipulation attacks show that GT-PD-L outperforms coordinate-wise trimmed mean by up to 4.3 percentage points under stealth attacks.

Multiagent Systems.title: Your Agents Are Aging Too: Agent Lifespan Engineering for Deployed Systems
Multiagent Systems.summary: Long-lived AI agents are increasingly deployed as persistent operational systems, yet they are still mostly evaluated like freshly initialized models. Day-one benchmarks miss a basic systems question: how does an agent's reliability change after deployment? Even when model weights are frozen, an agent's effective state keeps changing as it compresses interaction history, retrieves from a growing memory store, revises facts after updates, and undergoes routine maintenance. Reliability therefore becomes a lifespan property of the full agent harness, not only a snapshot property of the base model. We introduce AgingBench, a longitudinal reliability benchmark for agent lifespan engineering: measuring not only whether deployed agents degrade, but what form the degradation takes and where repair should target. AgingBench organizes agent aging into four mechanisms: compression aging, where writing and rewriting drops future-relevant details; interference aging, where accumulated similar memories crowd out the target fact; revision aging, where changed or derived state is not updated correctly; and maintenance aging, where lifecycle events such as model swapping trigger regressions. To diagnose these failures, AgingBench uses temporal dependency graphs and counterfactual probes that produce diagnostic profiles for the write, retrieval, and utilization stages of the memory pipeline. Across 6 scenarios, 10 memory systems and 6 models from two families, we find that agent aging is not one-dimensional over 400 runs spanning 50-200 sessions: a well-formed reply can hide a value the memory no longer supplies; derived state collapses as updates accumulate; and the same wrong answer can require different repairs depending on what the diagnostic profile points to.

Multiagent Systems.title: MultiTurnRoute: A Platform for Building and Evaluating Multi-Turn LLM Routers
Multiagent Systems.summary: In a multi-turn conversation, the choice of language model at one turn can affect which model should answer the next. The selected model's reply shapes the context for the next query, and its cached prompt prefix can reduce the cost of using that model again. We introduce MultiTurnRoute, a platform for building and evaluating multi-turn LLM routers. A shared interface gives built-in and user-defined routers the current query, dialogue history, and an estimate of each model's reusable prefix length. Our routing algorithm, Chain-of-Route (CoR), uses a learned gate over recent and recurrent dialogue history to predict response quality and estimates cost from each model's reusable prefix. MultiTurnRoute Arena ranks routers on recorded conversations and compares session quality and cost in interactive runs where a simulated user responds to each reply. On a benchmark drawn from WildChat and LMSYS-Chat-1M with per-turn quality annotations for five LLMs, CoR reduces the normalized cost required to match the strongest model's quality by up to 20.3% relative to the strongest routing baseline, while matching or improving peak response quality.

Multiagent Systems.title: A Gamified Framework for Conflict-Driven Design: Discovering Strategies for Collaborative Resilience with Multi-Agent Learning
Multiagent Systems.summary: Conflicting stakeholder objectives make it difficult to coordinate investments in urban resilience. We model conflict-driven urban design as a non-zero-sum digital board game in which stakeholder agents allocate scarce resources and balance individual payoffs against shared urban development and resilience objectives. We use multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) to train policies and examine their behavior across three settings. On a 4 x 4 board, learned policies reach about 84% of the total return found by a simulated annealing benchmark. On an 8 x 8 board with spatial and resource constraints, trained agents favor projects that improve resilience in self-play. In a 12 x 12 simulation initialized from historical maps of Tatsumi, Tokyo, trained agents achieve a mean total score of 452.1, compared with 357.3 for a random-policy baseline across 10,000 simulation runs. Gains in adaptability, sustainability, flood resistance, and greenery come with reductions in vitality and density. A human-in-the-loop interface supports replay and lets participants take over stakeholder decisions, providing a testbed for exploring these trade-offs in participatory urban planning.
Multiagent Systems.comment: 10 pages, 11 figures, 1 table. Author version of a paper published in the proceedings of ACADIA 2025: Computing for Resilience

Multiagent Systems.title: Selective Cooperative Perception via Blind Spot Reasoning and Agentic Dialogue with Vision-Language Models
Multiagent Systems.summary: Real-time cooperative perception (CP) in multi-agent traffic environments is highly resource-intensive, which posing scalability challenges for large-scale deployment. Efficiency can be significantly improved by selectively performing CP only in safety-critical scenarios and for key occluding objects. Vision-Language Models (VLMs) are well-suited for complex reasoning in dynamic and uncertain environments, making them a promising tool for this selective CP task. This study proposes a VLM-driven agentic framework for blind spot reasoning and dialogue-based CP. A mixed-model architecture is designed that integrates conventional object detection for stable perception, vision-language reasoning for identifying impactful occlusions, and a physics-based geometric module to align reasoning with real-world visibility constraints. The framework also incorporates a Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting mechanism to enhance interpretability and intent-aware decision-making. We collect real-world data from connected vehicles operating in urban traffic and compare the driving-critical blind spot identification and dialogue performance of four state-of-the-art VLMs. Experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves over 80% accuracy in driving-critical blind spot detection and over 90% success in dialogue-driven perception sharing. This work provides a scalable, interpretable, and bandwidth-efficient alternative to conventional CP pipelines, and offers new insights into agentic communication design for future connected traffic systems.

Multiagent Systems.title: Sensitivity Analysis of Decision Rules in an Agent-Based Agro-Ecological Model
Multiagent Systems.summary: Agent-based models are well-suited for modelling agro-ecological systems for decision-making, yet turning their simulations into actionable insight requires identifying which decisions actually drive the behaviours. In such a context, sensitivity analysis stumbles upon a structural feature of many complex systems: the parameters are not a flat vector but a decision tree in which many parameters appear only when a higher-level choice activates them. Classical global sensitivity analysis presupposes independent inputs over a fixed Cartesian product and is ill-posed on such a branched space and biased by construction. We instead treat the structure of the decisions as a first-class modelling object. Using advanced surrogate modelling techniques, we encode the crop-management itinerary of the high-resolution agro-ecological modelling platform MAELIA as a hierarchical design space featuring both categorical and numerical variables. We propose a novel dedicated method to analyse this kind of hierarchical space, a random-forest-supervised HSIC-ANOVA, which ranks main effects and interactions natively on the tree while placing rarely and always active decisions on an equal footing. We show how, when applied to simulation outputs such as nitrogen leaching, soil organic carbon variation, and yield predictions, it can deliver an interpretable, decision-oriented reading.

Multiagent Systems.title: Multi-Agent Conditional Diffusion Planning for Decentralized Wireless Resource Allocation
Multiagent Systems.summary: In wireless communication systems, efficient and adaptive resource allocation is essential for enhancing overall Quality of Service (QoS). Compared with conventional Model-Free Reinforcement Learning (MFRL), Model-Based RL (MBRL) first learns a generative world model for subsequent planning, enabling more stable training through the reuse of historical experience. However, deploying MBRL in large-scale wireless networks remains challenging due to high-dimensional stochastic dynamics, strong inter-agent cooperation, and stringent communication constraints. To overcome these challenges, we propose a Multi-Agent Conditional Diffusion Model Planner (MA-CDMP) for decentralized communication resource management. Following the Decentralized Training with Decentralized Execution (DTDE) paradigm, MA-CDMP models each communication node as an autonomous agent and employs Diffusion Models (DMs) to capture environment dynamics. An inverse dynamics model is further incorporated to guide action generation, improving sample efficiency and policy scalability. Moreover, to efficiently approximate large-scale agent interactions, we introduce a Mean Field (MF) mechanism to assist the classifier in conditional DMs. This mitigates inter-agent non-stationarity and enhances cooperation with minimal communication overhead. We further establish an upper bound on the distributional approximation error induced by MF-based diffusion generation, guaranteeing convergence stability and reliable modeling of multi-agent stochastic dynamics. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MA-CDMP consistently outperforms existing MARL baselines in terms of average reward and QoS metrics, showcasing its scalability and practicality for real-world wireless network optimization.

Multiagent Systems.title: Independent Learning of Nash Equilibria in Partially Observable Markov Potential Games with Decoupled Dynamics
Multiagent Systems.summary: We study Nash equilibrium learning in partially observable Markov games (POMGs), a multi-agent reinforcement learning framework in which agents cannot fully observe the underlying state. Prior work in this setting relies on centralization or information sharing, and suffers from sample and computational complexity that scales exponentially in the number of players. We focus on a subclass of POMGs with independent state transitions, where agents remain coupled through their rewards, and assume that the underlying fully observed Markov game is a Markov potential game. For this class, we present an independent learning algorithm in which players, observing only their own actions and observations and without communication, jointly converge to an approximate Nash equilibrium. Due to partial observability, optimal policies may in general depend on the full action-observation history. Under a filter stability assumption, we show that policies based on finite history windows provide sufficient approximation guarantees. This enables us to approximate the POMG by a surrogate Markov game that is near-potential, leading to quasi-polynomial sample and computational complexity for independent Nash equilibrium learning in the underlying POMG.

Multiagent Systems.title: What Do Collusion Probes Read? Three Pitfalls in Evaluating Multi-Agent Collusion Monitors
Multiagent Systems.summary: Activation probes look like near-perfect monitors for secret collusion among large language model (LLM) agents. We show that they mostly detect that an agent was told to collude, not that it decided to. Our benchmark (2,500 committee and 1,476 code-review episodes) adds agents who receive the collusion instruction and refuse it, separating instruction from decision. Published detectors barely tell colluders from these refusers, and our best probe separates them mostly by reading the instruction: without it, agent AUROC falls from 1.00 to 0.61. Two further pitfalls inflate reported results: scored after the vote, a rule that only reads the votes reaches AUROC 0.990 but finds nothing before it; and in 57% of attempts no colluder argues for the target in public. The decision is still there: a probe trained on agents' own choices reads it (AUROC 0.73 without the instruction), and probes find colluders whose goal was fine-tuned into the weights (AUROC 0.995; pre-registered). We turn the controls into a protocol for testing any collusion monitor, and adapt scan statistics into an online monitor for groups of any size.
Multiagent Systems.comment: 30 pages, 5 figures. Code: https://github.com/mainul3195/collusion-probe-pitfalls ; data: https://huggingface.co/datasets/mainul3195/collusion-probe-pitfalls ; archive: doi:10.5281/zenodo.23636508

Multiagent Systems.title: M3FT: Micro-Macro-Micro Reasoning for Multi-Agent Cryptocurrency Perpetual Futures Trading
Multiagent Systems.summary: Cryptocurrency perpetual futures form a large-scale online financial market in which automated agents manage interacting asset positions under changing conditions. Policies relying solely on micro-level numerical states may overlook cross-asset relationships and become vulnerable to regime shifts, while macro-level linguistic judgments alone cannot ensure precise measurement or optimize positions under trading costs and risk constraints. Connecting market interpretation to coordinated multi-asset decisions remains challenging. We propose M3FT, a micro-macro-micro framework for multi-agent perpetual futures trading. The first micro stage constructs time-aligned numerical states from exchange and account observations through deterministic processing. The macro stage transforms these measured states into explicit market interpretations without adding external market information. Four asset-specific teams, each comprising a Market Interpreter, an Asset Communicator, and a Risk Reviewer, refine these interpretations through experience retrieval, cross-asset communication, and review of joint-position risks. The final micro stage combines encoded linguistic representations with the original numerical states to learn continuous target positions. We implement this framework with a language-conditioned multi-agent policy: asset actors use global and private numerical states together with linguistic context, while centralized critics evaluate joint actions using portfolio-wide information and shared-account rewards. Experiments on real cryptocurrency perpetual futures data, including comparisons across language models and policy-learning algorithms and component ablations, show that the best-performing M3FT configuration achieves a higher mean test return than the evaluated direct LLM, numerical RL, and rule-based baselines.

Multiagent Systems.title: MAC-Bench: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Collaboration via Interconnected Tasks
Multiagent Systems.summary: Large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems (MAS) tackle challenging tasks by dividing work among agents and coordinating their contributions toward shared objectives. Evaluating these systems therefore requires benchmarks that assess not only task-solving performance but also the ability to handle interdependent work. However, existing benchmarks often emphasize task difficulty without substantial collaboration requirements or evaluate only a limited range of predefined collaboration patterns. In this paper, we introduce MAC-Bench, a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating multi-agent collaboration through interconnected tasks. Rather than imposing predefined agent roles or communication protocols, MAC-Bench embeds collaboration requirements directly into task dependencies and shared-resource constraints. Specifically, we mine reusable collaboration structures from selected benchmark tasks at two levels. Local collaboration patterns capture recurring interactions among subtasks, while global task structures characterize how these interactions contribute to complete workflows. Through coarse-to-fine composition, these structures are recombined into task graphs combining different collaboration requirements. Tasks are instantiated in executable environments with automated verification of partial progress and complete task resolution.

Multiagent Systems.title: FlowMAS: Learning Multi-Agent Workflow Topology via Information-guided Generative Flow Network
Multiagent Systems.summary: Automated multi-agent systems offer clear advantages over manually designed ones in scalability and adaptability, but existing workflow topology methods still face important limitations. Search-based methods are often computationally expensive, textual-gradient-based methods rely on coarse-grained feedback, and existing generation-based methods are not well suited to discrete workflow topologies with complex dependencies. To address these limitations, we propose FlowMAS, a multi-agent workflow topology method based on Generative Flow Networks (GFlowNets). FlowMAS models workflow generation as reward-guided flow over the topology space and introduces three components: a GFlowNet-based topology generation backbone, a curiosity-driven module for structure-aware exploration, and an information-guided optimization module for evaluating intermediate topologies. Concretely, the curiosity-driven module encourages exploration of structurally novel workflows, while the information-guided module measures both the information contribution and the communication efficiency of different operators to favor more informative and effective collaboration patterns. Experiments on six benchmark datasets with three LLM backbones show that FlowMAS consistently outperforms multiple baselines.

Multiagent Systems.title: Who Remembers What? Multi-Granularity Memory Extraction for Multi-User, Multi-Agent Interaction
Multiagent Systems.summary: Self-evolving agents improve their own skills, memory, and harness code from experience without retraining the base LLM, and group-evolving agents go further by sharing these lessons across agents. Yet most such systems overlook that sharing across users and heterogeneous agents requires deciding who can benefit from each lesson and what information must remain private. We present MixUA, a memory system that distills independent user-agent trajectories into lessons and assigns each lesson to a user-agent pair, user, agent, or global scope according to whom it benefits and what it may disclose. For evaluation, we introduce CrossLearnBench, a mixed-user-agent benchmark that pairs established agent tasks with user preferences and privacy probes that test whether private facts leak into memory other users can read. With five users and seven agents, MixUA raises pass rates by up to 16 points over no memory and 5 over a single global memory, even on tasks previously tried only by other users on other agents. It retains up to 90% of previously stated preferences, and at most 0.02% of privacy probes find a planted private fact in a forbidden scope. We hope MixUA offers a scalable path toward a global system where users and agents co-evolve.

Multiagent Systems.title: LAMaS: A Modular Platform for Learning Low-Latency Multi-Agent Orchestration
Multiagent Systems.summary: In a multi-agent system (MAS), removing an expensive agent call can save tokens without making the answer arrive sooner: latency depends on the longest chain of dependent calls. We present Latency-Aware Multi-agent System (LAMaS), a modular platform for learning low-latency orchestration. A framework can send a query to LAMaS and receive an answer and execution trace, or keep its own graph builder and use the platform's latency-optimized orchestration layer. During training, the layer gives operators on the critical path the greatest latency penalty while targeting a floor on expected accuracy. During inference, a lightweight controller uses partial results to decide whether to skip work that has yet to start. Across four benchmarks, LAMaS reduces end-to-end latency by over 50% relative to the evaluated learning-based MAS baselines while maintaining competitive or better accuracy. GDesigner and AgentDropout retain their graph builders and train the controller on their own traces; both achieve lower latency across the same benchmarks.
Multiagent Systems.comment: Preprint. Previously this version appeared as arXiv:2607.13359 which was submitted as a new work by accident

Multiagent Systems.title: SkillOps: Managing LLM Agent Skill Libraries as Self-Maintaining Software Ecosystems
Multiagent Systems.summary: Large language model agents increasingly rely on skill libraries for multi-step tasks, yet these libraries can accumulate persistent defects as skills are added, reused, patched, and linked to changing dependencies. We call this failure mode skill technical debt: library-level defects that may not break a single skill locally but can harm future retrieval, composition, and execution. Existing skill-based agents mainly focus on task-time retrieval, planning, and repair, while library-time maintenance remains underexplored. We propose SkillOps, a method-agnostic plug-in framework for maintaining skill libraries. SkillOps represents each skill as a typed Skill Contract (P, O, A, V, F), organizes skills with a Hierarchical Skill Ecosystem Graph, and diagnoses library health across utility, compatibility, risk, and validation dimensions. Given a raw skill library, SkillOps produces a maintained library that can be used by existing retrieval or planning agents without changing their internal code. On ALFWorld, SkillOps achieves 79.5 percent task success as a standalone agent, outperforming the strongest baseline by 8.8 percentage points with no additional task-time large language model calls. As a plug-in layer, it improves retrieval-heavy baselines by 0.68 to 2.90 percentage points. The current rule-based maintenance implementation uses nearly zero library-time large language model calls or tokens, showing that skill-library maintenance can be added as a low-overhead architectural layer.

Multiagent Systems.title: Finite-Sample Convergence in Networked Average Reward MARL: Decentralization Pitfalls and Entropy Remedies
Multiagent Systems.summary: We study the problem of average reward Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) where agents interact within a network. Each agent in the network conducts local updates with information within its $k$-hop neighborhood and collaboratively maximizes the overall reward of the entire network. We first provide impossibility results in achieving convergence to the global optimal joint policies in our setting. These impossibility results highlight the challenges of decentralized learning with local information in multi-agent systems, namely the issues of multiagency, where each agent independently optimizes its policy, and partial observability, where agents have limited visibility into the global state. Given these challenges which indicate that decentralized policy optimization can generally be certified only up to stationarity, we provide finite-sample convergence guarantees for a decentralized actor-critic algorithm with linear function approximation that converges to an approximate stationary point with small gradient norm. To overcome such impossibility results, we further show that adding fixed-state entropy regularization reshapes the objective landscape which leads to even stronger global convergence guarantees for our proposed actor-critic algorithm.

Multiagent Systems.title: LSRP*: Scalable and Anytime Planning for Multi-Agent Path Finding with Asynchronous Actions
Multiagent Systems.summary: Multi-Agent Path Finding (MAPF) seeks collision-free paths for multiple agents from their respective starting locations to their respective goal locations while minimizing path costs. Although many MAPF algorithms were developed, most of them rely on a common assumption on synchronized actions, where the actions of all agents start at the same time and always take a time unit. This assumption may limit the use of MAPF planners in practice. To get rid of this assumption, recently, an algorithm called Loosely Synchronized Rule-based Planning (LSRP) was proposed, which can find sub-optimal solutions for many agents. However, LSRP often finds poor quality solutions due to its unbounded sub-optimality. This paper develops a new anytime planner called LSRP* that can keep improving solution quality after the initial solution is obtained until the runtime budget depletes. We analyze the properties of LSRP* and test it against several baselines with up to 1000 agents on various maps. LSRP* can handle up to 25% more agents than LSRP and can reduce up to 40% of the solution cost found by LSRP.

Multiagent Systems.title: Scale-Dependent Collective Adaptation in Self-Amending LLM Societies: A Cross-Family Study of Emergent Governance
Multiagent Systems.summary: We study group decision-making in artificial societies where the rules of play are themselves subject to collective amendment. Using the self-amending game Nomic, we compare multiple scales across two LLM families and find that collective adaptation does not improve monotonically with model size. Instead, both families exhibit a narrow mid-scale regime that supports sustained rule adoption, diverse amendments, and balanced consensus. Smaller models tend to remain rule-inert, whereas larger models often converge on restrictive voting patterns, and heterogeneous mixed-size groups collapse into veto-driven gridlock. These cross-scale contrasts persist under temperature perturbations and under a shift from unanimity to majority voting, although latent-state structure varies by family and scale. Hidden-state divergence alone does not explain collective performance: high representational divergence can coincide with poor behavioural outcomes. Linear probes reveal regime-selective coupling between latent vote-predictive signals and collective behaviour, but decodability is necessary rather than sufficient for adaptive play. Overall, the recurring regularity is non-monotonicity, not the particular scale at which the optimum appears. Self-amending games therefore provide a controlled testbed for studying collective adaptation in artificial societies beyond raw model scale.

Multiagent Systems.title: Measuring What Tool-Using LLM Agents Actually Do: Structured Validation, Causal Error Propagation, and Fabricated Tool Use
Multiagent Systems.summary: Tool-using agents built on large language models (LLMs) are usually scored by comparing the final answer with a reference text, using a string heuristic or an LLM judge. This is unreliable when the references describe the task rather than its answer. We replace it with a deterministic validator that checks the tools called, the executed parameters, the resulting state, and whether the values in the answer are supported by the correct tool observations. We re-scored 33,583 traces from 13 agents on simulated calendar, weather, medical and retail tools. The simulator reproduced all 10,396 logged observations, and the gold observations supported the validator in 16 of 18 disagreements with a three-annotator majority (the annotators in none). The instrument changes conclusions: on the same 306 traces, Gemini-2.0-Flash scores 63.4% under the substring heuristic and 5.6% under the validator. In a paired design (same task and model, with and without one schema-valid wrong argument injected into the first tool call), the error rate rises from 52.4% to 74.5% (+22.0 percentage points, 95% CI 18.4-25.5; 1,085 pairs, 7 models), and by 44.7 points (38.4-51.0) where the corrupted call executed without errors. An LLM-judge ensemble estimates +2.5 points on the same pairs. Agents also report tool results without executing any call, in 0-42.5% of traces depending on the model (rule-based lower bounds), largely because the harness accepts an action and a final answer in one completion. A rule-based runtime monitor costs about 7 microseconds per trace but reduces wrong answers mainly by abstaining.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Convergence of Byzantine-Resilient Gradient Tracking via Probabilistic Edge Dropout
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: We study distributed optimization over networks with Byzantine agents that may send arbitrary adversarial messages. We propose Gradient Tracking with Probabilistic Edge Dropout (GT-PD), which combines a universal self-centred projection that clips incoming messages to a radius-$τ$ ball around the receiver with a fully decentralized probabilistic dropout rule driven by a threshold-gated, dual-metric trust score in the decision and tracking channels. These identity-free defences bound adversarial perturbations while preserving doubly stochastic mixing. The projection preserves the honest network average exactly in every realization, even when honest messages are clipped. Under complete Byzantine isolation ($p_b=0$), GT-PD converges linearly to a neighbourhood of order $ασ^2/(μn_{\mathcal H})$ plus higher-order network terms, matching centralized stochastic gradient descent to first order in the step size. We also give a radius computable from problem data that ensures honest messages remain unclipped with high probability. Under partial isolation ($p_b>0$), a leaky variant, GT-PD-L, controls accumulated tracking perturbations and converges linearly to a bounded neighbourhood governed by stochastic variance and the clipping-to-leak ratio, under explicit conditions on the step size, leak, and aggregate Byzantine mixing weight. With two-tier dropout and $p_h=1$, Byzantine isolation adds no variance to honest consensus dynamics. MNIST experiments under Sign Flip, ALIE, and Inner Product Manipulation attacks show that GT-PD-L outperforms coordinate-wise trimmed mean by up to 4.3 percentage points under stealth attacks.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: An Interline Multiport DC Circuit Breaker with Power Flow Controller
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Currently, the high-voltage multi-terminal DC (MTDC) grids face two major challenges. First, fast rise rate and lack of zero-crossing point in DC-side fault currents render AC circuit breakers inoperable. Second, DC line currents are passively determined by terminal DC voltages and line resistances, which inherently limits the capability of changing individual line currents for essential grid services such as power flow management and overloading prevention. To address these two limitations, DC circuit breakers (DCCBs) and DC power flow controllers (DCPFCs) have been developed. The conventional DCCBs are two-port devices installed in series with DC lines at their terminals in an MTDC converter substation, so that any fault current flowing through the line can be rapidly cleared. Additionally, a DCPFC can be installed at line terminals to adjust terminal voltages and power exchanges among adjacent lines. As a result, for a substation that connects to multiple lines, it needs to host multiple DCCBs and a DCPFC, which significantly increases the cost and footprint of both the substation and the MTDC grid. To this end, this work proposes an integrated equipment combining multiple DCCBs and a DCPFC, called the interline multiport DCCB with DCPFC, which can reduce the number of components and enhance the economic feasibility of MTDC networks. This paper presents the topology, operation principles, and component selection procedures of the proposed equipment, and compares it with the state-of-the-art technologies. Electromagnetic transient (EMT) simulation results validate the fault interruption and power flow control performance of the interline multiport DCCB with PFC.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Challenges in the Proper Metrological Verification of Smart Energy Meters
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: The most common instruments currently used to measure active/reactive energy and power quality indicators are smart energy meters (EM). Unfortunately, the verification of such meters is currently performed under ideal conditions or with simple signal models, which do not recreate actual states occurring in the power grid and do not ensure the verification of the properties of their signal chains. This paper presents challenges in proper metrological verification of smart EM. It presents existing legal and normative requirements and scientific research directions regarding these meters. Although the meters tested comply with the normative and legal requirements, the results reveal numerous imperfections in the signal and measurement chains for the selected test signal. Based on the results of the research results, further directions have been determined in the field of smart EM.
Systems and Control (EESS).comment: 5 pages, 5 figures, submitted to IEEE conferences: 2026 22nd International Conference on Harmonics & Quality of Power (ICHQP)

Systems and Control (EESS).title: BRACE: Belief-guided Residual Adaptive Control for Safe Navigation under Unknown Disturbances
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Disturbances encountered during autonomous navigation generally vary across space, often discontinuously, as obstacles redirect wind and changing terrain alters traction. Tracking controllers typically assume sufficient control authority to mitigate disturbances and maintain safety; the regime where this assumption fails remains underexplored. We present Belief-guided Residual Adaptive Control (BRACE), a hierarchical reinforcement learning (RL) framework for reach-avoid navigation under unknown, bounded, spatially varying disturbances. BRACE infers a disturbance belief from model prediction errors and uses that to condition a high-level policy that adapts the reference trajectory. The policy combines a nominal and a belief-guided residual term, trained jointly with a likelihood-ratio advantage reweighting heuristic. We evaluate BRACE in three simulated quadcopter environments with abruptly switching wind fields, and validate it on Crazyflie hardware with fan-generated disturbances. Across these settings, BRACE improves reach-avoid performance over model predictive control and RL baselines.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Clustered Randomized Smoothing for Stochastic Prediction Functions
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Modern stochastic predictors can model rich, multi-modal outcome distributions. However, this expressive power comes with challenges in ensuring robust predictions $-$ a critical requirement in safety-critical domains. Randomized smoothing is a leading technique for improving robustness, particularly against adversarial perturbations. Yet, in stochastic multi-modal regression settings, randomized smoothing often fails due to mode collapse, yielding averaged predictions that do not reflect the underlying distribution. To address this limitation, we propose clustered $α$-smoothing, a framework that (1) partitions noisy samples using an arbitrary clustering algorithm, (2) applies $α$-smoothing locally within each cluster, and (3) combines the resulting predictions into a mixture distribution. By interpreting the smoothing distribution as a mixture of $α$-smoothers, we derive a lower bound on the probability that the smoothed prediction lies within a union of compact regions corresponding to distinct modes. We empirically evaluate our framework on two benchmarks, demonstrating substantial improvements over state-of-the-art methods. In stochastic trajectory prediction on a driving simulator dataset, our approach achieves, on average, a $27\%$ lower Wasserstein distance to the ground-truth distribution compared to $α$-smoothing. In quadrotor control, where modes correspond to distinct feasible paths to a target, our method reduces the collision rate by $90\%$ relative to the state-of-the-art randomized smoothing.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Bisect-Index-Choose: A Fast and Exact Algorithm for EV Charging under Minimum Charging Rates
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Electric vehicle (EV) charging stations are increasingly operated with an aggregate power limit below the sum of their port ratings, and require scheduling algorithms to divide the available power among the connected EVs. Charging standards permit a current that is either zero or at least a minimum rate, typically 6 A, which makes this allocation problem non-convex. Existing methods either solve a mixed-integer program with a commercial solver, which can be computationally expensive, adds software dependencies, and incurs licensing costs, or apply heuristics without optimality guarantees. This paper proposes Bisect-Index-Choose (BIC), a fast and solver-free scheduling algorithm that computes a globally optimal allocation among EVs under mild assumptions on their utilities. For $n$ EVs, BIC runs in $O(n \log n)$ time when all EVs share one maximum rate and in $O(n^2)$ time for two, times a logarithmic factor in the numerical precision. In tests with up to 1000 EVs, BIC attains global optimality and is up to three orders of magnitude faster than the solver. On real-world charging data, it needs less capacity and delivers more energy than existing heuristics. We implement BIC on a low-cost microcontroller and show that it solves instances with 1000 EVs in less than 90 ms.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Computationally Efficient Data Generation for Learning Nonlinear MPC Policies
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Learning MPC requires large datasets generated by repeatedly solving MPC problems. For Nonlinear MPC (NMPC), dataset generation is computationally expensive because feasible initial states are difficult to sample efficiently. The feasible set is often non-convex or even disconnected, and many randomly sampled states are infeasible, leading to wasted optimization solves and unnecessary computational effort. In this work, we propose a data-generation framework for learning NMPC policies that combines active-set exploration with projection-based sampling. First, a bilevel formulation samples activity weights to promote solutions associated with different active sets while preserving optimality for the original NMPC problem; second, a simpler slack-based formulation uses weighted slack variables to target different active sets at the single level. These reference solutions are then used to construct local linearized feasible sets, from which candidate initial states are sampled and projected through the nonlinear NMPC problem to recover feasible and locally optimal training samples. Our approach is up to $37\times$ faster than baseline uniform sampling with $99\%$ acceptance rate, while maintaining a representative coverage of the feasible set.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Sampling-based Model Predictive Control as Sequential Monte Carlo Inference
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Sampling-based model predictive control (MPC) is treated as a family of distinct algorithms: predictive sampling, MPPI, the cross-entropy method, and their biased, colored-noise, and annealed variants all sample control sequences and reweight them by cost. We show a single Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) inference algorithm implements them all, specified by three independent axes: the proposal, the update rule that reduces cost-weighted particles to a nominal plan, and the effective-sample-size threshold for resampling. We evaluate SMC-based planning on MuJoCo non-linear control, open-loop navigation through obstacle fields, 7-DoF motion planning, and non-prehensile push-T, in simulation and on a Franka FR3. Resampling combats particle degeneracy at long horizons. At a 28-knot horizon in our navigation domain it cut the collision rate by 30% over non-resampling baselines. Programmable proposals improve push-T success over perturbative baselines, improving from 1% to 100% in simulation and 10% to 90% on hardware.
Systems and Control (EESS).comment: 8 pages, 5 figures. Submitted to IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (RA-L). Code: https://github.com/CoMMALab/PFMP

Systems and Control (EESS).title: A Nested Heterogeneous Multiscale Framework for Power System Dynamic Simulation
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Power system dynamics involve multiple timescales, from electromagnetic transients of the network and inverter-based resources to electromechanical oscillations of synchronous generators and quasi-steady-state evolution of the operating point. Simulating these dynamics with a detailed electromagnetic transient model is computationally prohibitive, whereas existing methods reduce the model to focus on a single timescale and lose accuracy when dynamics of different timescales interact. This paper proposes a nested heterogeneous multiscale framework for highly efficient multi-timescale simulation of a power system represented by one unified detailed model. Rather than varying only the integration step, the framework adaptively shifts the simulation resolution among three nested levels so that the dynamics of interest at each stage are always captured, with the slower dynamics estimated on the fly from short detailed simulations at controlled accuracy. Theoretical analysis proves the stability of long steps during quasi-steady-state evolution and quantifies the attainable speedup. On a modified IEEE 39-bus system with frequency regulation and load restoration, the framework accurately reproduces the dynamics of all timescales and runs 15 to 18 times faster than conventional simulation of the detailed model. The accuracy and speedup of the proposed method are further verified on a 390-bus system, demonstrating its scalability to large power systems.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Modified CNN-Learned Surrogate Covariance With Krylov/Lanczos Subspace for DoA Estimation
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Recently, learning-based approaches have been employed to improve the robustness of subspace methods in DoA estimation. A Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) was used as a data-driven framework employing an autoencoder to generate a well-conditioned surrogate covariance optimized end-to-end through a differentiable classical estimator, such as the Root-MUSIC. The complete system is designed to estimate the directions of arrival based on a spectral decomposition using the EVD of this covariance matrix. In this work, a new approach is proposed by formulating the spectral stage of the Root-MUSIC algorithm in terms of the orthogonal complement of the signal subspace, thereby eliminating the need for the noise subspace and noise eigenvalues. Furthermore, the full EVD is replaced by a Lanczos tridiagonalization with reorthogonalization, reducing the overall computational cost.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Real-Time Threat Classification in Multi-Agent Systems via Topology-Coupled Hidden Markov Models
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Networked multi-agent systems coordinating in adversarial environments face compound cyber threats that alternate between false-data injection (FDI), denial-of-service (DoS), and stealthy decoy perturbations designed to mimic benign operational anomalies. Because the switching policy is latent and the plant dynamics evolve continuously, deterministic threshold detectors struggle to isolate deception without causing excessive false alarms. This paper presents an online, data-driven framework that couples distributed continuous time unknown input observers (UIOs) with a topology-aware Hidden Markov Model (HMM) for real-time attack detection and classification under unknown adversarial strategies. By decoupling FDI signals from augmented node states, distributed observers deployed across the network generate local augmented residuals that are discretized into emission sequences. The HMM embeds the underlying directed communication graph into the off-diagonal blocks of its transition probability matrix, explicitly capturing inter-agent attack propagation. Both transition and observation probabilities are updated recursively online via an Expectation-Maximization (EM) scheme, adapting the classifier to evolving threat behaviours without prior offline calibration. Numerical simulations on a directed network demonstrate that incorporating graph topology into the latent transition dynamics resolves the severe classification ambiguity between nominal and decoy modes, outperforming decoupled agent-independent decoders while restricting observer deployment to a sparse subset of nodes.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Passivity-Guaranteed Variable Impedance and Compliance Control via Online Parameter Optimization
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Variable impedance control enhances the interaction capability of robot manipulators by adapting impedance parameters online. However, time-varying impedance parameters may inject energy into the system and violate passivity, particularly when tasks demand rapid stiffness changes. Existing methods address this by increasing damping or limiting the stiffness profile, which often degrades the dynamic response. In this work, we propose a quadratic programming-based parameter optimization framework that guarantees passivity by modulating the desired inertia to compensate for energy injected by stiffness variations, while preserving a critically damped system. For the case of diagonal impedance matrices, we optimize the rates of change of inertia and stiffness subject to a passivity constraint formulated as a convex quadratic program. We extend the framework to compliance control, where the desired inertia is coupled to the robot's configuration-dependent inertia matrix. We use an eigendecomposition based on Cholesky factorization to optimize the spectral weights while maintaining passivity. Experiments on the Kinova Gen3 7-degree-of-freedom manipulator validate both methods with human interaction perturbations. Comparisons with an energy tank approach and a nonpassivity-based method demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves less conservative stiffness tracking without requiring an energy reservoir or damping overhead.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Deep Reinforcement Learning with Massively Parallel Simulation for Low-Thrust Multi-Revolution Rendezvous
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: The growing demand for on-orbit servicing and constellation management in low Earth orbit requires autonomous and reliable low-thrust rendezvous. Traditional numerical methods struggle with the long-horizon nature of multi-revolution maneuvers under perturbations, while standard deep reinforcement learning (DRL) methods are limited by low simulation throughput and poor sample efficiency. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a massively parallel DRL guidance framework. A fully tensorized, GPU-resident orbital propagator is developed to integrate $J_2$-perturbed orbital dynamics and policy optimization within a zero-copy pipeline, achieving up to a 67-fold increase in simulation throughput over conventional CPU baselines. In addition, the rendezvous problem is formulated in modified equinoctial elements and trained with a progressive curriculum learning strategy to improve convergence and generalization across increasingly challenging rendezvous scenarios. Simulations show that the proposed framework can learn robust rendezvous trajectories for complex multi-revolution rendezvous over a broad range of orbital configurations. Additional evaluations under a high-fidelity model and eclipse-induced thrust interruptions further demonstrate the robustness of the learned policy under practical mission constraints. Moreover, the trajectories generated by the proposed framework can be used as effective initial guesses for optimization-based trajectory solvers, improving the convergence of high-precision trajectory optimization. The method offers a scalable approach for real-time low-thrust guidance and trajectory optimization.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Two-Timescale Trajectory Control, Task Reassignment and Resource Scheduling for Multi-UAV Cooperative Mobile Edge Computing
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV)-assisted mobile edge computing (MEC) is a promising technology, leveraging the advantages of UAVs including flexible deployment, wide coverage, and reliable wireless communication. In this paper, we study the task reassignment and offloading problem in a multi-UAV cooperative operating environment, and consider the real occurrence that the computing tasks arrive more frequently than UAVs make flight decisions. In addition, we also take into account the position offset of the UAV during flight and the unavailability of the UAV due to external interference. We propose a two-timescale optimization framework, where the trajectory of the UAV is carried out on a large timescale, while the task reassignment and computing resource allocation are jointly optimized on a small timescale. The core objective is to maximize the long-term average system gain, which takes both energy consumption and task delay into account. To address the UAV trajectory optimization problem under large timescale constraints, we propose a constrained multi-agent deep reinforcement learning algorithm. For decision-making within small timescale, to jointly optimize task offloading decisions and computing resource allocation, we integrate convex optimization with a heuristic algorithm. Finally, we conduct extensive simulations to evaluate the proposed algorithms against the baseline, achieving a 24% reduction in latency and a 28% reduction in total system cost.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Decision-Dependent Stochastic Optimization: The Role of Distribution Dynamics
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Distribution shifts have long been regarded as troublesome external forces that a decision-maker should either counteract or conform to. An intriguing feedback phenomenon termed decision dependence arises when the deployed decision affects the environment and alters the data-generating distribution. In the realm of performative prediction, this is encoded by distribution maps parameterized by decisions due to strategic behaviors. In contrast, we formalize an endogenous distribution shift as a feedback process featuring nonlinear dynamics that couple the evolving distribution with the decision. Stochastic optimization in this dynamic regime provides fertile ground to examine the various roles played by dynamics in the composite problem structure. To this end, we develop an online decision-making algorithm that both adapts to and shapes the dynamic distribution. Throughout the paper, we adopt a distributional perspective and demonstrate how this view facilitates characterizations of distribution dynamics and the optimality and generalization performance of the proposed algorithm. We showcase the theoretical results in an opinion dynamics context, where an opportunistic party maximizes the affinity of a population with evolving, polarized opinions, and in a recommender system scenario, featuring performance optimization with discrete distributions in the probability simplex.
Systems and Control (EESS).comment: Published in the Journal of Machine Learning Research

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Worst-Case Contagion in Financial Networks: MILP Clearing and Robust Loss Analysis
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: We study worst-case contagion losses in financial networks with interbank liabilities and common exposures to marketable assets. Existing linear-programming approaches provide exact stress-test values only within an insolvency-resilience margin, where all institutions remain solvent with respect to the external sector. We show that this margin is computed exactly by a finite family of linear programs, one per vertex of the uncertainty ball, whereas a single linear program based on the componentwise worst deterioration of external resources yields only a certified lower bound. We extend this framework beyond that margin in three directions. First, we derive an exact mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) formulation for the maximal clearing vector under arbitrary signed external net positions, providing a clearing oracle for robust stress testing when insolvency can occur. Second, we develop certified bounds on the worst-case loss beyond the margin, including insolvency-pattern enumeration, scenario lower bounds, fixed-pattern dual upper bounds, localized certificates, and a regime-generation procedure with monotone gap certificates. Third, we analyze the worst-case loss curve as a function of the perturbation radius. For $\ell_1$ and $\ell_\infty$ price-perturbation sets, the curve is convex, nondecreasing and piecewise linear up to the margin, with breakpoints generated by switches in worst-case shock directions, LP bases, and bank-level activity patterns. Beyond the margin, it remains nondecreasing and piecewise affine, but convexity may fail, the curve may jump upward, and the worst case need not be attained. The framework provides a certifiable MILP/LP methodology for parametric stress testing and interpretable diagnostics identifying the banks responsible for changes in systemic loss.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: From Discrete Snapshots to Geometric Entity: Motion-Native Channel Tracking for THz Near-Field XL-MIMO
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Channel tracking in mobile terahertz (THz) near-field extremely large-scale multiple-input multiple-output (XL-MIMO) systems is challenging because spherical-wave propagation couples angle and range, leading to rapid and nonlinear channel evolution under sparse pilot observations. Existing approaches typically estimate pilot-local channel or position snapshots before applying temporal tracking or smoothing, making them vulnerable to information loss during snapshot formation. To break this bottleneck, we propose a paradigm shift from tracking discrete snapshots to estimating a holistic geometric entity, namely, one shared continuous UE trajectory over the tracking window. Specifically, we parameterize the trajectory using a low-dimensional cubic B-spline representation and directly couple the per-pilot profile likelihoods through this shared trajectory before any pilot-local position estimate is finalized, thereby inducing continuous near-field channel evolution. We further characterize the efficient geometric information supplied by each pilot observation and its aggregation in the shared spline-coefficient space. Based on this formulation, we develop a regularized maximum a posteriori estimator and a quadratic-penalty lifted solver that separates parallel pilot-local geometric updates from a structured global spline update. The resulting global system is banded and, for a fixed spline degree, admits linear-complexity factorization, enabling an efficient structured implementation. Simulations demonstrate consistently improved tracking accuracy over representative temporally refined baselines in the tested medium-to-high-SNR regime, together with a favorable accuracy--runtime trade-off. These results highlight the benefit of coupling sparse pilot observations through a shared continuous trajectory rather than temporally processing independently estimated snapshots.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Shifted Interaction Functions: A Unified Framework for Imperfect Actuation and Sensing in Consensus Networks
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: Practical networked robotic systems rarely implement ideal consensus interactions exactly, since local actuation constraints, sensing biases, and heterogeneous interaction maps may shift the input-output relations used by distributed controllers. Rather than focusing solely on whether consensus occurs, such imperfections can fundamentally alter the structure of the asymptotic collective behavior, typically yielding global or clustered velocity alignment, while exact static agreement arises only in special cases. This paper develops a shifted-interaction framework for analyzing collective alignment under imperfect actuation and sensing. Shifted functions provide a compact representation of local actuator and sensor maps, allowing actuation constraints and sensing biases to be represented by horizontally and vertically shifted monotone interactions. The framework distinguishes nodal shifted actuation from edge-wise shifted sensing. For shifted actuation, a Lyapunov analysis establishes global velocity alignment under compatible actuation ranges, including bounded, non-invertible, and deadzone-type maps. For shifted sensing, a maximum-principle argument and a paired-sensitivity condition establish convergence to velocity clusters over edges with infinite accumulated sensitivity; uniform sensing sensitivity yields exponential global velocity alignment. In the linear case, closed-form expressions characterize asymptotic behavior and identify actuation as a special case of sensing. Simulations illustrate static, globally aligned, and clustered velocity-aligned behaviors.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Online Geometric Consistency Assessment of LiDAR Measurements via Recursive Bayesian Comparison
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: LiDAR-based localization and mapping systems produce registered point clouds that serve as geometric measurements for downstream estimation and navigation. Registration errors introduce duplicated surfaces and structural deformation into these measurements. In the absence of an independent reference, online assessment relies on geometry accumulated from earlier measurements. Such assessment requires tolerance to sampling variation and an accumulation process in which observations enter the history only after evaluation. We therefore formulate a recursive Bayesian comparison that couples geometric assessment with history maintenance. A Normal-Inverse-Wishart model represents historical voxel geometry and its uncertainty, while a weak isotropic reference adapts to current sampling. Comparing the marginal predictive support of the same current points under both models yields Normalized Drift Evidence (NDE). Assessment precedes assimilation: positive NDE triggers an alarm and preserves the preceding historical state; otherwise, the current observations update the history. Across 14 real-world sequences totaling approximately 73 min from four platform types, alarms identified all nine corrupted sequences and were absent from all five consistent sequences. In four representative scenarios with event references, first alarms occurred within 0.9 s of the reference times, with no preceding alarms. Cross-backend evaluation demonstrates consistent responses to reconstructed geometry. Ablation and controlled perturbation results establish the roles of uncertainty modeling, recursive history, displacement, and geometric support. Mean processing time is 4.2--6.1 ms per update at 1 Hz. In ten UAV trials, alarms initiated odometry isolation, landing, relocalization, and mission continuation.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Balancing Confidentiality and Attack Detectability in Networked Control Systems over Lossy Wireless Channels
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: We study the joint protection of a networked control system (NCS) against eavesdropping and data integrity attacks over a lossy wireless channel. The eavesdropper intercepts the transmitted sensor measurements and control inputs to reconstruct the system state. In contrast, the integrity attacker in this study replaces the sensor measurements with fabricated data to drive the system to undesired operating conditions. Although these two threats are typically studied separately, a wireless NCS should be protected against both simultaneously, and a defence against one affects the other. We employ an observation-encoding scheme that renders the eavesdropper's state-estimation error covariance unbounded under packet drops, and show that transmission energy governs how long this error remains bounded. In particular, lower transmission energy improves confidentiality. For integrity protection, we combine stochastic physical watermarking with a CUSUM-based sequential change detector. The proposed attack detection scheme accounts for intermittent communication and encoded measurements. The detection delay is governed by the Kullback--Leibler divergence (KLD) between the pre- and post-attack distributions of the test signal, and we show that a higher transmission energy increases the KLD and thereby reduces the detection delay. Furthermore, we derive analytical expressions for the eavesdropper's estimation error and the worst-case expected KLD, providing guidelines for selecting transmission energy to balance confidentiality and integrity protection and characterising the privacy--security trade-off. Finally, we run numerical simulations to validate our theoretical findings and demonstrate the privacy--security trade-off in practical scenarios.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: On Real Eventual Exponential Positive property of complex-valued Laplacians and their pseudoinverses
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: The property of real eventual exponential positivity guarantees the state trajectories of a linear time-invariant system to evolve asymptotically to right half of the complex-plane [1]. It has applications in the characterization of herdability and reachability of states in networked systems. Networks with complex-valued edge-weights arise in AC power systems and opinion dynamics. Recent work has introduced real eventual exponential positive (rEEP) Laplacians, for which the trajectories of the associated network flow eventually converge to consensus. We establish further properties of rEEP Laplacians and their pseudoinverses. Firstly, we show that the rEEP property for complex-valued matrices exhibits invariance under specific rotational transformations. Secondly, we establish that the property of rEEP is preserved under the MoorePenrose pseudoinverse operation, highlighting its robustness under algebraic manipulations. These results apply to effective impedance computation in AC networks and to consensus in multi-agent systems. Finally, we provide numerical examples to validate our theoretical results.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Dynamic State Estimation from Sparse PMUs via Physics-Informed Graph Neural Operators
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: This paper proposes a physics-informed graph neural operator for power system dynamic state estimation. From a sparse, intermittent measurement window at a few generator buses, the operator estimates the rotor-angle and speed trajectories of all machines, unmeasured ones included, in one forward pass. A graph-attention encoder processes the measurements, and the swing equations are imposed as a hard constraint or as a soft one with a learned correction that absorbs model errors. It is trained on simulated measurements, without state labels. With several phasor measurement units, masked training hides one from the input but keeps it in the loss. On four transmission systems, simulations show that the operator is the most accurate estimator that neither optimizes per scenario nor uses state labels, except on the smallest system at large model errors, where tuned Kalman smoothers are better. Networks trained on simulated states are more accurate on the two smallest systems but not on the 118-bus system, where the operator is faster and more accurate than hard-constrained moving-horizon estimation. Under model errors, it matches or outperforms an optimization-based benchmark at a fraction of its cost. The results hold for a detailed machine model with exact parameters seen only through voltage phasors.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: On asymptotic stability of the time-varying Kalman filter for unstabilizable linear systems: an optimization perspective
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: This paper establishes the necessary and sufficient conditions for asymptotic stability of the time-varying Kalman filter applied to a linear time invariant system with semidefinite initial state covariance and positive definite process and measurement noise. Rather than analyze the discrete Riccati equation as in the classic literature, the equivalent state smoothing optimization problem is stated and all results are established using properties of this optimization problem. A Lyapunov-like function, termed a modified $Q$-function is derived and used for this analysis. This optimization approach removes the need for the classic but cumbersome Riccati iteration algebra and provides better generalization and application for nonlinear systems.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: Simulating Nonlinear Resistive Networks using a Behavioral Splitting
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: An operator splitting method is developed for computing operating points of nonlinear resistive networks. Our behavioral formulation separates the device laws from Kirchhoff's laws and casts simulation as a zero-finding problem. Branch port resistances then provide a diagonal preconditioner for the relaxed Peaceman-Rachford iteration in scattering variables. Each iteration requires solving independent scalar equations and a linear system with a fixed weighted Laplacian matrix. Convergence is established for maximal monotone device laws when an operating point exists. Contractive branch reflections also yield a linear convergence bound independent of network topology. Numerical experiments on crossbar arrays illustrate the computational advantages.

Systems and Control (EESS).title: From Winding-Fault Geometry to Reliability: Estimation and Prognosis of Stator Inter-Turn Faults
Systems and Control (EESS).summary: This paper develops an integrated framework for estimation, prognosis, and reliability assessment of stator inter-turn faults in induction motors. The fault is characterized by its severity, defined as the fraction of short-circuited turns, and its spatial orientation. A geometric fault model shows that the resulting output signature is affine in the fault severity and exhibits a fundamental spatial periodicity. Exploiting this structure, an augmented-state particle filter jointly estimates the nonlinear electromechanical state and the unknown fault severity while quantifying posterior uncertainty. The estimated degradation is then propagated using four prognostic models: linear trend, Holt exponential smoothing, Bayesian degradation, and particle-based forecasting. Their predictions are connected to threshold-crossing remaining useful life (RUL), first-passage reliability, degradation-dependent hazard reliability, and a Weibull lifetime benchmark, thereby providing both deterministic and probabilistic health assessments. Numerical results demonstrate accurate online fault estimation and output reconstruction, characterize the effects of degradation pattern and prediction horizon on prognosis, and show consistent reliability and threshold-crossing predictions. Moreover, estimation accuracy remains comparable across the distinct fault orientations induced by the spatial periodicity. The resulting framework provides a unified connection from physics-based inter-turn fault modeling to online diagnosis, degradation prognosis, and reliability assessment.

Robotics.title: Awomo-SimDataEngine: Agentic Simulation-ReadyWorld Generation
Robotics.summary: Generating useful robot-training data requires more than visually plausiblescenes: objects must support interaction, placements must remain physicallyvalid, and tasks must admit repeatable execution. We present\textbf{Awomo-SimDataEngine}, an agentic system that connects asset and scenegeneration to robot demonstration synthesis.
